This position will offer you the opportunity to manage the execution of multiple transmission, substation and distribution projects. The position will involve coordinating with multiple internal and external departments to manage the life cycle of capital project execution.

Responsible for project execution, contract administration, planning and resource management

7+ years of experience in Project Management of Utility, Construction, Engineering, or other relevant experience

Experience in capital project management
Experience with serving as a firm/client liaison in a support or lead role
Ability to multitask and manage multiple competing priorities is critical to success

Ability to work in a collaborative team setting
A high school diploma or GED

jobs.description:
BearCom is the largest distributor of wireless voice, data, and video solutions in North America, and North America's largest two-way radio channel partner for Motorola, with more than 40 years of industry leadership, partnerships with leading manufacturers including JVC Kenwood and Avigilon, and a network of 75+ branches across North America. Together, BearCom and Stone Security deliver communication, technology, and security solutions that help organizations operate safely, efficiently, and effectively – offering customers scalable solutions and employees the platform to build meaningful, high-impact careers.

We are currently seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Project Manager to join our growing team

Job Description

The Project Manager is responsible for the initiation, planning, execution, supervision, and implementation of projects related to the customers' objectives. Responsibilities also include proactively identifying project risks and mitigation strategies for those risks, building, maintaining, and tracking project schedules, capturing, categorizing, and identifying the resolution of project issues.

Job Responsibilities And Duties

Exceptional communication with all stakeholders, external and internal
Oversee project progression from inception to completion, including permits, material delivery, contracting, managing subcontractors, etc.
Understanding of project scope and completing projects on time and within budget
Maintains installation schedules and coordinates task scheduling with other trades
Troubleshoot project issues and engage appropriate resources as needed to mitigate impacts
Plans and schedules engineering, installation, and subcontracting activities of assigned projects
Manage multiple small to large-scale projects simultaneously across the Southeast without supervision.
Manage project budget and project profitability
Manage and execute project change orders
Extensive travel is required

Qualifications

Must have 5+ years of security and project management experience
Ability to engage with all levels of management
Individuals will be technically inclined, have good written and verbal communication skills, be self-motivated, be dependable to work under little supervision, and be eager to learn.
Must have experience in the construction field and security industry
Proficient with MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Project, and SharePoint).
Strong technical knowledge of relevant technology and tools, i.e., access control, video surveillance, and intrusion.
Experience in LenelS2 and Milestone preferred
Basic understanding of TCP/IP networking

Benefits

Stone wants to elevate your professional growth! We value investing in developing our team members and advancing your technical capabilities. Stone can provide extensive on-the-job training and covers all fees associated with most professional certifications.

You’ll Also Receive

Highly Competitive Compensation
Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
Company-Paid Life, Short Disability Insurance
Paid Holidays
Generous Paid Time Off
Matching 401k Plan
Use of Company Vehicle
Employee Referral Bonus

jobs.description:
Requirements

Description & Requirements

Maximus is hiring a Sr. Project Manager - Pursuit Operations to lead and coordinate strategic opportunities through the full pursuit lifecycle, ensuring teams stay aligned, risks are managed, and key milestones are achieved. This role serves as a central point of coordination across complex, cross-functional pursuits, driving accountability, maintaining governance processes, and supporting timely decision-making.

The ideal candidate is a strong project leader with experience managing complex initiatives, coordinating diverse stakeholder groups, and tracking progress against critical deadlines. Success in this role requires exceptional organizational skills, sound judgment, and the ability to thrive in fast-paced environments while balancing multiple priorities. The successful candidate will leverage technology and approved AI-enabled tools to improve efficiency, strengthen collaboration, and increase visibility into milestones, risks, and action items across the pursuit lifecycle.

Why Maximus?

🔄 Work/Life Balance Support - Flexibility tailored to your needs!
💰 Competitive Compensation -Bonuses based on performance included!
🛡️ Comprehensive Insurance Coverage - Choose from various plans, including Medical, Dental, Vision, Prescription, and partially funded HSA. Additionally, enjoy Life insurance benefits and discounts on Auto, Home, Renter's, and Pet insurance.
🌟 Future Planning - Prepare for retirement with our 401K Retirement Savings plan and Company Matching.
🏝️ Unlimited Time Off Package - Enjoy UTO, Holidays, and extended sick leave, along with Short and Long Term Disability coverage.
🌱 Holistic Wellness Support - Access resources for physical, emotional, and financial wellness through our Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
🏆 Recognition Platform - Acknowledge and appreciate outstanding employee contributions.
📚 Tuition Reimbursement - Invest in your ongoing education and development.
🎁 Employee Perks and Discounts - Additional benefits and discounts exclusively for employees.
🌟 Maximus Wellness Program and Resources - Access a range of wellness programs and resources tailored to your needs.
📚 Professional Development Opportunities-Participate in training programs, workshops, and conferences.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Manage opportunities across the full pursuit lifecycle and lead cross-functional project teams through readiness milestones.
Own integrated project plans, governance routines, milestone schedules, risk registers, action logs, and executive status reporting.
Coordinate across operations, IT, pricing, HR, finance, proposal, sales, and internal stakeholders to maintain progress against pursuit timelines.
Monitor schedule health, milestone readiness, unresolved actions, decision delays, and risk exposure across assigned opportunities.
Escalate risks, issues, and decision needs with clear impacts, owners, timing, and recommended next steps.
Promote practical use of approved AI-enabled tools to improve workflow efficiency, automate routine coordination tasks, and strengthen visibility into action status, milestones, and risks.
Run after-action reviews and translate lessons learned into pursuit management, governance, and tracking improvements.

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor's degree in relevant field of study and 7+ years of relevant professional experience required, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Program Requirements:

Specialized experience needed: hands-on management of complex pursuits, proposals, implementations, or other deadline-driven projects with multiple workstreams, dependencies, governance routines, and executive visibility.
Candidates should be advanced users of integrated project plans, milestone schedules, readiness trackers, RAID logs, action registers, decision logs, and executive status reporting.
Must have strong cross-functional coordination experience across operations, IT, pricing, HR, finance, sales, proposal, SMEs, and leadership stakeholders.
Must communicate clearly, escalate early, and use approved AI-enabled tools to streamline notes, action tracking, reporting, and risk visibility.
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail skills needed

This position is fully remote and will require a home office.

Home office requirements:

Reliable high-speed internet service

Minimum 20 Mpbs download speeds/50 Mpbs for shared internet connectivity

Minimum 5 Mpbs upload speeds

EEO Statement

Maximus is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, genetic information and other legally protected characteristics.

Pay Transparency

Maximus compensation is based on various factors including but not limited to job location, a candidate's education, training, experience, expected quality and quantity of work, required travel (if any), external market and internal value analysis including seniority and merit systems, as well as internal pay alignment. Annual salary is just one component of Maximus's total compensation package. Other rewards may include short- and long-term incentives as well as program-specific awards. Additionally, Maximus provides a variety of benefits to employees, including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, a retirement savings plan, paid holidays and paid time off. Compensation ranges may differ based on contract value but will be commensurate with job duties and relevant work experience. An applicant's salary history will not be used in determining compensation. Maximus will comply with regulatory minimum wage rates and exempt salary thresholds in all instances.

Accommodations

Maximus provides reasonable accommodations to individuals requiring assistance during any phase of the employment process due to a disability, medical condition, or physical or mental impairment. If you require assistance at any stage of the employment process—including accessing job postings, completing assessments, or participating in interviews,—please contact People Operations at applicantaccom@maximus.com

jobs.description:
We are seeking an entry-level, analytically-oriented Associate Project Manager to join our team! Our ideal candidate is someone who thrives in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, and takes initiative to seek out information, knowledge, and development, proactively. He or she is a resourceful problem solver who is savvy with technology and finds effective and efficient solutions to complex client problems. The Associate Project Manager is a true self-starter who deals well with uncertainty and ambiguity. Lastly, he or she is a proven team player who puts the success of the team first.

Responsibilities Include (but Are Not Limited To)

Work as part of a cross-functional project team responsible for the delivery of Interactive Response Technology (IRT) for randomization and drug supply management in clinical trials
Support the Services Delivery project team in:
Liaising with the client to discuss requirements, handle issues, provide status updates, and answer questions
Designing the IRT solution to meet the study requirements based on the clinical protocol, Suvoda proposal and discussions with the client
Accurately and completely documenting all requirements and participating in internal and external specification review meetings
Assisting with client review meetings of IRT specifications and supporting documents, making any required updates
Managing project schedules and scope, tracking all internal and client tasks required to meet project milestones
Managing the cross-functional project team’s schedule and task assignments
Assisting with creating the UAT plan, developing test scripts, coordinating data setup, and providing client support for client UAT
Providing protocol-specific support to the client and support team after go-live

Ensure client satisfaction throughout the project build and maintenance phase, working with Suvoda management, the Suvoda product team, and business development as needed
Provide system training to end-users using in-person meetings, web meetings, and user manuals
Provide telephone and email support to system users globally
Travel to client sites to attend meetings and conduct user training sessions
Perform other related duties as required

Requirements

Bachelor's degree (in life sciences or computer science preferred)
Interpersonal and communication skills
Time management and organizational skills
Analytical thinking ability
Creative problem-solving ability
Attention to detail

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Webflow is the agentic web marketing platform for modern marketing teams, helping organizations build, manage, and optimize high-performing web experiences that drive predictable growth and strengthen brand trust. Building at Webflow will need grit, because we move fast, without ever sacrificing craft or quality.

We’re looking for a Staff Technical Program Manager, Emerging Products to help us take the next generation of Webflow, new AI-native products, from prototype to general availability and build the execution systems that let Webflow launch new products predictably.

About The Role

Location: Remote-first (United States)
Full-time
Permanent
Exempt
The cash compensation for this role is tailored to align with the cost of labor in different geographic markets. We've structured the base pay ranges for this role into zones for our geographic markets, and the specific base pay within the range will be determined by the candidate’s geographic location, job-related experience, knowledge, qualifications, and skills.
United States (all figures cited below are in USD and pertain to workers in the United States)

Zone A: $212,500 - $255,000

Zone B: $200,000 - $240,000

Zone C: $186,700 - $224,000

Canada (figures cited below are in CAD and pertain to workers in ON & BC, Canada)
232,000 - 278,000 CAD

This role is also eligible to participate in Webflow's company-wide bonus program. Target amounts are a percentage of base salary and vary by career level. Payouts are based on company performance against established financial and operational goals.

Please visit our Careers page for more information on which locations are included in each of our geographic pay zones. However, please confirm the zone for your specific location with your recruiter.

Application Information:
Application deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis until position is closed and filled
This posting is for a new position
Reporting to the Senior Director, EPD Operations

As a Staff Technical Program Manager, Emerging Products, you’ll…

Own the execution portfolio for an emerging product line from discovery through GA, across multiple engineering pods and cross-functional workstreams spanning Engineering, Product, Design, and GTM.
Partner with Engineering leaders, Tech Leads, and PMs to decompose ambiguous, high-risk technical challenges into clear milestones, sequencing, and execution plans that drive toward abstract goals.
Design and run the operating model for a fast-moving, zero-to-one program: pod structure, DRI cadences, cross-functional leads syncs, readiness checklists, and leadership reviews that read from artifacts teams already produce rather than creating new reporting.
Define GA and launch readiness criteria with Product, Engineering, and GTM, and drive the trade-off decisions needed to hit them, with a named owner and decision date for each.
Anticipate risks and dependencies across pillars, establish proactive risk management, and give executives data-driven visibility into where the program actually stands.
Build repeatable systems, health metrics, and playbooks that outlive this program and become the default for how Webflow takes new products to market, embedding AI tooling and automation to scale visibility and reduce manual coordination.
Coach EMs, PMs, and peer TPMs on execution craft and ownership behaviors, raising the quality of program management around you.

Requirements

About you:

BS / BA college degree or relevant experience
7+ years of experience in technical program management, with a proven track record of running strategic, cross-pillar programs

You’ll thrive as a Staff Technical Program Manager, Emerging Products if you:

Have taken a new product from zero to launch, or led programs in an incubation, new-venture, or emerging-technology environment where scope, staffing, and requirements were still being defined.
Have a strong technical foundation and are comfortable partnering with technical leaders on architecture trade-offs and execution structure. Experience with AI, agentic, or developer platform products is strongly preferred.
Have built repeatable systems (operating cadences, readiness frameworks, health metrics) that improved execution beyond a single program and were adopted by others.
Are hyper-organized and capable of coordinating across multiple independent work streams and organizations without losing the thread.
Thrive in ambiguity: you frame trade-offs, facilitate prioritization, and bring forward recommended solutions rather than open questions.
Are a role model for effective execution practices, driven by an attuned sense of priority and urgency, and able to say the hard thing with care.
Communicate effectively with executives and engineers alike, and are a confident presenter to leadership teams and large internal groups.
Are proficient with program management tooling (e.g., Linear, Jira, Confluence, Google Suite) and able to introduce lightweight processes that scale.
Stay curious and open to growth — demonstrating a proactive embrace of AI, and actively building and applying fluency in emerging technologies to elevate how we work, drive faster outcomes, and expand collective impact.

Our Core Behaviors

Build lasting customer trust. We build trust by taking action that puts customer trust first.
Win together. We play to win, and we win as one team. Success at Webflow isn't a solo act.
Reinvent ourselves. We don't just improve what exists, we imagine what's possible.
Own it all the way. We move fast because the moment demands it, and we hold ourselves accountable to deliver outcomes — for each other, and for customers.

Benefits

Ownership in what you help build. Every permanent Webflower receives equity (RSUs) in our growing, privately held company.
Health coverage that actually covers you. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for full-time employees and their dependents, with Webflow covering most premiums.
Support for every stage of family life. 12 weeks of paid parental leave for all parents and 6+ weeks of additional paid leave for birthing parents. Plus inclusive care for family planning, menopause, and midlife transitions.
Time off that’s actually off. Flexible vacation, paid holidays, and a sabbatical program to help you recharge and come back inspired.
Wellness for the whole you. Access to mental health resources, therapy and coaching.
Invest in your future. A 401(k) with 100% employer match (up to $6,000/year) in the U.S., and support for retirement savings globally.
Monthly stipends that flex with your life. Localized support for work and wellness expenses — from Wi-Fi to workouts.
Bonus for building together. All full-time, permanent, non-commission employees are eligible for our annual WIN bonus program.

Temporary employees may be eligible for paid holiday and time off, statutory leaves of absence, and company-sponsored medical benefits depending on their Fixed Term Contract and their country/state of employment.

jobs.description:
Summary

We are partnered with a mission-driven environmental consulting firm focused on sustainability and environmental impact that's seeking an Air Quality Project Manager
to join their growing team in Texas
. Their work focuses on supporting clients across traditional industries (oil&gas, petrochemical) as well as emerging sectors(data centers, renewables) to solve complex environmental challenges.

In this role, you will lead the technical delivery of air quality permitting and compliance projects while serving as a primary point of contact for clients throughout the project lifecycle. You will manage projects from initial scoping and proposal development through technical execution, regulatory review, and final delivery, ensuring projects are completed on time, within budget, and to a high technical standard.

This is an opportunity for an experienced air quality professional looking for greater project ownership, client interaction, and autonomy within a collaborative technical team. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in Texas air permitting and compliance, excellent project management skills, and the ability to build trusted relationships with clients.

This position is hybrid in Texas
or can be remote
for individuals not located near an office.

Key Responsibilities

Lead air quality permitting and compliance projects from initial scope through final deliverable, managing technical execution, schedules, budgets, and project objectives.
Serve as the primary client point of contact, managing communication, expectations, project updates, and deliverables throughout the project lifecycle.
Manage projects involving NSR, PSD, Title V, PBRs, Standard Permits, emissions inventories, and regulatory compliance.
Develop project scopes, work plans, budgets, schedules, proposals, and technical deliverables.
Interpret and apply TCEQ and federal air quality regulations to develop effective permitting and compliance strategies.
Coordinate with clients, regulatory agencies, and internal technical teams to resolve complex permitting and compliance issues.
Review technical work and deliverables for quality, accuracy, and regulatory compliance.
Identify project risks, manage changes in scope, and proactively communicate schedule, budget, and technical considerations to clients.
Mentor junior staff and provide technical guidance on air quality permitting and compliance projects.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Atmospheric Science, or related field.
5+ years of experience in air quality consulting, permitting, and compliance.
Strong experience with Texas air quality regulations and TCEQ permitting requirements.
Experience with NSR, PSD, Title V, PBRs, Standard Permits, and emissions inventories.
Project management experience, including scope, budget, schedule, and technical delivery.
Strong client management and communication skills with the ability to manage relationships throughout the project lifecycle.
Experience mentoring or providing technical guidance to junior staff is a plus!

Benefits

Health, dental, and vision insurance
Unlimited vacation time, 10 company holidays, & sick leave
Employee stock units with a public company
401(k) with company match
Hybrid (Monday Tuesday in-office) or remote work options
Strong professional development and promotion track

Job Description

PLEASE NOTE: Preferred location for the successful candidate is near our Cleveland, OH, Wichita, KS, Wheeling, WV, Kalamazoo, MI, or La Grange Park/Chicago, IL locations. However, we invite qualified applicants from any US location.

Congregational Operations Project Manager (Full-Time, Exempt)

Do you have progressively responsible project-management or project-coordination experience involving multiple locations, capital projects, real estate, energy, construction, or organizational transitions? Do you bring demonstrated success coordinating cross-functional stakeholders, consultants, contractors, and vendors, as well as strong skills in budgeting, scheduling, documentation, problem-solving, and written reporting?

If so, we invite you to read on...

Under the guidance of the Chief Operating Officer, the Congregational Operations Project Manager, works with Center Administrators, Leadership Partners, Facilities Staff, and Sisters to move forward the mission of the Congregation as it relates to facilities, operations, environmental and sustainability issues and other tasks.

Essential Functions

The Project Manager supports the Congregation of St. Joseph by coordinating projects that advance responsible stewardship of the Congregation's people, properties, financial resources, and care for creation.
This role will assist and support the operations of the Congregation. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and collaborating with all constituents of the Congregation over six different locations.
The role will collaborate closely with Congregational ministry staff including CSJI, CSJM, Center Administrators, Sisters, Leadership Partners, staff, consultants, and vendors.
This position manages capital improvements for several buildings, solar and energy initiatives, Sister moves, and other assigned operational projects across Congregation locations.
The role establishes clear scopes, schedules, budgets, responsibilities, risks, and measurable outcomes; provides timely progress reports and recommendations; and promotes safe, cost-effective, sustainable, and mission-aligned results.
In every assignment, the Project Manager is expected to foster respectful relationships, inclusive collaboration, discernment, accountability, and compassionate attention to the needs and dignity of the Sisters and the wider community.

Key Responsibilities

Collaborate with the Chief Operating Officer, CSJI representatives, Center Administrators, facilities staff, and other stakeholders to define project scopes, budgets, schedules, responsibilities, risks, and deliverables for approved projects.
Plan and coordinate Sisters' residential transitions, including moves from homes or apartments to Congregation-sponsored Centers; work sensitively with Sisters, families, landlords, movers, Center staff, and other service providers.
Manage a portfolio of assigned capital, facility, energy, environmental, real estate, and operational projects from planning through completion, maintaining project plans, schedules, budgets, decision logs, status reports, and closeout documentation.
Coordinate maintenance and capital-improvement projects for Congregation-owned retreat house, and several buildings and residences, while relying on qualified staff, consultants, and contractors for technical execution.
Coordinate requests for proposals, vendor evaluation, contracting, purchase approvals, and vendor performance in collaboration with the COO, CSJI, facilities personnel, finance, legal counsel, and other designated stakeholders.
Coordinate the Congregation's solar initiative and related sustainability projects, including feasibility work, site coordination, utility and incentive processes, contracts, implementation schedules, vendors, and progress reporting.
Lead the support existing energy procurement and energy efficiency projects; including utility and energy contracts, building system improvements, conservation initiatives and coordination with technical advisors and vendors.
Working closely with the COO to support the sale or other disposition of Congregation-owned properties by coordinating inspections, repairs, cleanouts, appraisals, brokers, legal and financial documentation, and closing-related activities.
Prepare concise project updates and recommendations for the COO and other decision-makers, promptly escalating risks, decisions, budget variances, and schedule concerns; perform other projects and operational assignments as directed.
The role may evolve over time to include coordinating building deconstruction or site restoration projects, including due diligence, regulatory requirements, and stakeholder communication while relying on professionals in the industry.
This role will be a member of multiple committees as assigned, including Leadership Partners, Forced Pooling and COSJ Capital Budgets.
Other duties as assigned.

Desired Skills

Project leadership: ability to organize scope, schedules, budgets, dependencies, risks, decisions, communications, and closeout across multiple concurrent assignments.
Technical and business literacy: ability to review proposals, contracts, plans, budgets, reports, and technical recommendations and translate them into clear choices for decision-makers.
Collaborative stakeholder and vendor management, including clear accountability, timely follow-up, constructive problem-solving, and concise status communication.
Empathy, discretion, and respect when coordinating projects that affect Sisters' homes, belongings, routines, and transitions.
Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence, with the ability to build effective working relationships with the COO, CSJI, Sisters, Center leadership, staff, professional advisors, and external partners.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare project plans, meeting notes, executive summaries, recommendations, and decision-ready reports.

Sensitivity to and respect for the CSJ Congregation's culture and values.
Ability to communicate effectively and clearly.
Ability to assess, define and resolve problems by identifying causes, gathering information, establishing facts, generating viable solutions, and recommending options to the parties involved or as needed.
Ability to think strategically by assessing options based on trends and conditions, as well as the Mission and values of the Congregation.

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in project management, business administration, construction management, engineering, real estate, environmental studies, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience will be considered.
Five to seven years of progressively responsible project-management or project-coordination experience, preferably involving multiple locations, capital projects, real estate, energy, construction, or organizational transitions.
Demonstrated success coordinating cross-functional stakeholders, consultants, contractors, and vendors; strong skills in budgeting, scheduling, documentation, problem-solving, and written reporting
Ability to understand and coordinate technical, contractual, regulatory, and property-related information; working knowledge of building systems, permits, codes, construction, utilities, or real-estate transactions is helpful but direct maintenance expertise is not required.
Valid driver's license and ability to travel regularly to Congregation-sponsored Centers, residences, and project sites.
Documented experience managing at least three concurrent projects with defined scopes, budgets, schedules, milestones, and stakeholder reporting.
Demonstrated experience managing individual project budgets of at least $250,000 or a comparable portfolio of capital and operational projects; experience with larger, multi-site initiatives is preferred.
Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, including Excel, Word, Outlook, Teams, and PowerPoint, and with a project-management or work-tracking platform used to maintain schedules, task ownership, risks, and status reports.
Ability to analyze bids, contracts, invoices, budgets, schedules, and change requests; identify material differences and risks; and present a clear written recommendation to the COO and other decision-makers.
Demonstrated ability to produce accurate project documentation and executive-level written reports, facilitate meetings, track decisions and action items, and communicate effectively with varied stakeholders.
Ability to handle confidential information with discretion and to coordinate projects affecting Sisters, their homes, and their belongings with sensitivity, respect, and alignment with the Congregation's Mission, Charism, Generous Promises, and Sacred Work.

Working Conditions

Standard office setting; hybrid, remote.
Engage in normal office activity, including lifting up to 25 lbs.
Preferred location near our Cleveland, OH; Wichita, KS; Wheeling, WV; Kalamazoo, MI; La Grange Park, IL locations.
Travel: travel to centers, Sister residences and other project sites as needed.

Physical Activity Requirements

Ability to conduct site walks, attend inspections, and support move days that may involve lifting light items and extended standing.
Able to stand for long periods of time, lift up to 25 lbs., and ability to travel.
Periodic evening or weekend work.

Salary: Competitive salary commensurate with experience.

jobs.title: Tech Infra Program Manager, Non-Standard Infrastructure Delivery (NSID)
jobs.description:
Description

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.

You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

About The Role

The AWS Non-Standard Infrastructure Global Delivery Team builds and scales infrastructure for AWS programs that don't fit neatly into traditional data center models. Our projects are tailored to the specific needs of internal and external customers — from satellite ground stations that downlink data from orbit, to specialized labs where engineers develop custom silicon and push the boundaries of quantum computing, to purpose-built environments with precision environmental controls for archival storage systems, to infrastructure that extends the AWS network to the furthest edge of its global footprint. Each program brings its own constraints, its own technical requirements, and often its own first-of-kind design challenges.

What makes this team unique is the degree of ambiguity we operate in. Many of our projects begin as loosely defined requests from internal customer teams who know what they need to accomplish but not necessarily what infrastructure it takes to get there. A significant part of this role is working upstream with those customers to develop initial requirements, define technical scope, build demand forecasts, and refine scaling models — often for infrastructure types where no established playbook exists. The solutions we deliver are boutique by nature: custom-designed to meet specific programmatic needs, site constraints, and operational models that vary from project to project.

The scope is broad, the problems are novel, and the pace of growth means we are constantly onboarding new infrastructure types and scaling models.

If you thrive in ambiguity, enjoy the challenge of translating vague asks into engineered solutions, and want to shape how AWS builds and scales its infrastructure globally — this role is for you.

We have an immediate opening for a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager III to drive capacity delivery across multiple non-standard infrastructure programs worldwide. You will lead cross-functional teams through the full lifecycle of infrastructure delivery — from upstream requirements definition and demand forecasting through design development, procurement, construction, commissioning, and deployment. You will develop and implement scalable mechanisms for tracking program health, drive data-driven decisions influencing significant capital investments, and work with stakeholders across AWS to solve constraints, remove blockers, and accelerate delivery.

Your Work Will Span

Requirements development — Working with internal customer teams to translate ambiguous needs into defined technical requirements, scope documents, and infrastructure specifications for novel deployment types
Stakeholder management and influence — Navigating complex, matrixed organizational structures and influencing without authority to align diverse teams, secure resources, drive decisions, and maintain momentum across programs where no single team owns the end-to-end outcome
Demand forecasting and capacity planning — Building initial demand models and scaling forecasts for programs where historical baselines don't exist, and refining them as programs mature
Boutique design coordination — Partnering with engineering teams to develop tailored infrastructure solutions that meet unique programmatic constraints (environmental, regulatory, physical, operational)
Multi-year delivery execution — Driving complex, globally distributed projects from conceptual feasibility through budget approval, design, procurement, construction, and commissioning
Cross-program coordination — Identifying synergies, shared solutions, and lessons learned across a diverse portfolio of infrastructure types
Mechanism development — Building scalable processes and reporting to monitor delivery health, drive accountability, and escalate to leadership as the portfolio grows

This role offers an opportunity to drive and influence business-critical decisions impacting the long-term future of AWS, working at the leading edge of emerging capability and service offerings. You must be comfortable managing remote project teams delivering novel — and sometimes pioneering — solutions across multiple countries and time zones; operating as the connective tissue between customer teams with undefined needs and engineering teams who build solutions; assessing and mitigating downstream risk; troubleshooting unforeseen implementation issues; removing barriers to project success; and operating effectively amid persistent uncertainty and change.

Up to 15% domestic and international travel may be necessary to support AWS non-standard infrastructure planning and scaling efforts.

Key job responsibilities

Work upstream with internal customer teams to elicit, define, and document technical requirements for infrastructure programs that are often undefined or loosely scoped at inception
Develop initial demand forecasts and capacity scaling models for emerging programs; refine forecasts as programs mature and data becomes available
Lead end-to-end delivery of boutique infrastructure projects from requirements definition through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and deployment
Manage project budgets, schedules, and resource plans for programs with diverse and evolving technical requirements and site conditions
Partner with engineering teams to develop tailored infrastructure solutions — working within unique constraints that vary by program, site, and customer need
Coordinate cross-program activities to gain cost and execution efficiencies; identify and drive shared solutions and reusable design patterns
Build and maintain relationships with internal customers (service teams, lab teams, engineering organizations) to align infrastructure delivery with evolving demand
Convene partners and stakeholders to architect end-to-end process flows, delineate roles and responsibilities, and establish governance frameworks — transforming ambiguity into operational clarity, eliminating friction, and driving repeatable efficiencies across maturing programs
Identify and mitigate risks in environments with limited precedent; develop contingency plans for first-of-kind deployment scenarios
Develop scalable mechanisms, standard operating procedures, and process improvements to support rapid portfolio growth and new program onboarding
Create data visualization reports and KPIs illustrating program health; escalate issues with clear recommendations to executive leadership

A day in the life

No two days are the same. You might start the morning in a requirements-definition session with a lab team that has a new hardware validation need but no infrastructure spec — helping them articulate what they actually need built. Then you shift to reviewing a demand forecast for a program expanding into new geographies, working with limited data and a lot of assumptions to refine. After lunch you're troubleshooting a procurement constraint on a boutique design that doesn't fit standard ordering mechanisms, followed by a cross-functional review of site conditions for a deployment in a venue that's never hosted this type of infrastructure before. You'll also spend time convening partners and stakeholders to architect process flows, delineate roles and responsibilities, and establish governance frameworks — transforming ambiguity into operational clarity, eliminating friction, and driving repeatable efficiencies across maturing programs. You'll regularly work with finance to secure capital, partner with engineering to translate customer intent into buildable designs, and look downstream to identify risks before they become blockers. The variety is the appeal — and the ability to navigate ambiguity, define scope where none existed, and drive delivery across technically diverse programs is what makes this role unique.

About The Team

The Non-Standard Infrastructure team exists because AWS's growth doesn't stop at the walls of traditional data centers. We deliver capacity for programs whose infrastructure needs are unique, evolving, and often undefined at the outset. Our work starts upstream — helping customer teams figure out what they need — and carries through to handing over operational infrastructure that meets exacting requirements we helped define. Our team members are builders and translators: people who can sit with a scientist, engineer, or service owner, understand what they're trying to achieve, and turn that into a deliverable infrastructure program. If you're energized by variety, comfortable building the plane while flying it, and motivated by the impact of enabling AWS's most innovative services — you'll fit right in.

Experience identifying, mitigating, and managing business risks and tradeoffs
Experience identifying and mitigating project risks in ambiguous or unprecedented deployment environments

3+ years of directly managing and being responsible for multiple large projects experience

Track record of building program management mechanisms from scratch to support a growing and diversifying portfolio of project types
Strong data analysis skills; experience building dashboards and metrics to drive program health visibility
Familiarity with AWS infrastructure concepts, data center design principles, or cloud computing architecture

The successful candidate will partner closely with customers, sales, solution architects, engineers, implementation teams, and executive stakeholders to deliver high-impact AI and infrastructure initiatives.

This is a senior individual contributor role focused on direct program leadership, execution excellence, and technical delivery oversight across strategic customer programs.

Develop and maintain comprehensive program plans, roadmaps, delivery schedules, resource plans, and governance frameworks.

Manage multiple complex workstreams simultaneously while maintaining program-level visibility and accountability.

Customer Engagement & Delivery

Technical Planning & Execution

Program Controls & Governance

Monitor program schedules, budgets, resource utilization, milestone completion, and delivery quality.
Facilitate RAID management for risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies.
Manage change requests, scope adjustments, decision logs, and customer communications.
Establish repeatable delivery frameworks, templates, and technical program management best practices across customer engagements.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a seasoned technical program leader who thrives in customer-facing environments, can translate complex technical initiatives into structured delivery plans, and has a proven track record of successfully leading enterprise AI, infrastructure, and transformation programs.

This individual is equally comfortable engaging with customer executives, architects, engineers, vendors, contractors, and delivery teams while driving programs from vision through execution.

This role offers the opportunity to lead high-visibility customer AI and infrastructure programs while establishing disciplined, scalable technical program management practices.

Behaviors and Competencies

Integrated Program Planning: Can develop and manage comprehensive program plans, roadmaps, delivery schedules, resource strategies, and governance frameworks while aligning technical execution with business objectives and customer expectations across complex initiatives.
Budget & Resource Tracking: Can monitor program budgets, resource utilization, project health, and delivery milestones, while proactively identifying risks to financial and resource commitments and ensuring accountability across teams.
Technical Roadmap Development: Can translate business goals, customer requirements, and technical strategies into actionable roadmaps that guide execution, align stakeholders, and support successful program delivery.
Critical Path & Dependency Management: Can identify, manage, and communicate complex dependencies, critical path activities, and cross-functional risks, ensuring effective coordination and minimal disruption to delivery timelines.
Architecture & Readiness Reviews: Can facilitate architecture reviews, technical assessments, readiness checkpoints, and implementation validation activities to ensure projects are properly planned and prepared for execution.
Release, Cutover & Transition Planning: Can lead deployment strategies, release planning, cutover execution, operational readiness activities, and transition-to-support processes while minimizing business and customer impact.
Requirements & Acceptance Criteria: Can collaborate with technical and business stakeholders to define requirements, establish acceptance criteria, validate deliverables, and ensure successful outcomes aligned with customer expectations.
SOW Execution & Scope Control: Can manage Statements of Work (SOWs), track contractual deliverables, maintain scope discipline, evaluate change requests, and ensure commitments are delivered within agreed parameters.
Vendor & Contractor Coordination: Can effectively coordinate work across vendors, contractors, implementation partners, and internal teams while maintaining accountability, communication, and alignment to program objectives.
Executive Governance & Reporting: Can develop executive dashboards, program scorecards, governance materials, and strategic communications that provide leadership visibility into program performance, risks, and outcomes.
RAID & Change Management: Can proactively identify and manage risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies, and change requests while driving resolution strategies and maintaining program stability throughout the delivery lifecycle.
Customer Stakeholder Management: Can build trusted relationships with customer executives, business leaders, technical stakeholders, and delivery teams while effectively managing expectations, facilitating decision-making, and driving successful customer outcomes.

Skill Level Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, Business, or a related field.
10+ years of experience leading complex technical programs and enterprise technology initiatives.
Demonstrated experience managing customer-facing SOW-driven projects from project kickoff through final delivery.
Proven experience leading large-scale infrastructure, cloud, AI, data center, or technology transformation projects.
Exceptional customer-facing communication and stakeholder management skills.
Experience working directly with executive sponsors, technical leaders, engineering teams, vendors, and customer stakeholders.
Strong command of integrated program planning, critical path management, dependency mapping, RAID management, change control, and executive reporting.
Ability to translate technical architecture, requirements, and implementation constraints into clear program plans and customer-facing communications.
Hands-on experience with Asana and Airtable; experience with Microsoft Project, Jira, Confluence, or comparable enterprise delivery tools.
PMP (Project Management Professional) certification required.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience delivering AI, machine learning, data platform, or advanced technology initiatives.
Experience supporting infrastructure deployments, data center implementations, and cloud migrations.
Experience supporting large-scale onsite facility buildouts, data center construction projects, infrastructure deployment programs, and coordination across facilities, construction, engineering, networking, power, cooling, and operational readiness teams.
Familiarity with Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and hybrid infrastructure environments.
Scrum Master, SAFe, Agile, or related certifications.
Consulting, professional services, or systems integration experience.
MBA or advanced technical degree preferred.

Other Requirements

Customer-facing role requiring direct engagement with customers, executive stakeholders, vendors, contractors, engineering teams, architects, implementation teams, and delivery organizations.
Ability to lead large-scale AI, infrastructure, cloud, data center, networking, storage, modernization, and technology transformation programs.
Ability to manage multiple complex workstreams while maintaining delivery accountability across scope, schedule, budget, quality, and customer success criteria.
Strong leadership in governance, risk management, issue resolution, resource coordination, and organizational alignment.
Ability to establish and scale repeatable technical program management practices, frameworks, templates, and governance processes across customer engagements.

Your morning starts with program health checks - tracking dependencies, partner commitments, and what's at risk before it becomes a blocker. By mid-morning you're in technical architecture discussions with engineering leads, surfacing hidden risks and ensuring today's decisions don't create problems six months out. Afternoons bring vendor negotiations, stakeholder narratives, and cross-functional working sessions to unblock stalled dependencies. Your customers are the engineers who need unblocked programs, the PMs who need their roadmaps sequenced, and ultimately the millions of Amazon customers whose social CS experience depends on the infrastructure you're keeping on track.

CS-Social is Amazon's global team dedicated to delivering exceptional customer service across all social media apps. We monitor and respond to customers, solving problems, escalating systemic issues, and positively engaging with millions of customers worldwide. Our team of associates operates across multiple countries and time zones.

As a Sr TPM, you'll work directly with senior leadership to shape the strategic direction of social customer service at Amazon. You'll mentor other team members, influence engineering roadmaps across multiple organizations, and have the autonomy to drive decisions that impact how customers experience Amazon globally.

jobs.description:
At Sonos we want to create the ultimate listening experience for our customers and know that it starts by listening to each other. As part of the Sonos team, you’ll collaborate with people of all styles, skill sets, and backgrounds to realize our vision while fostering a community where everyone feels included and empowered to do the best work of their lives.

The Software Operations team designs, builds, and continuously improves the operating systems that help Sonos software teams plan, develop, measure, and deliver great products. As a Technical Program Manager on this team, you won't be assigned to a single program to run meetings and track status — instead, you'll work across the software development organization to improve how engineering itself works. You'll help build an AI-enabled software development lifecycle, improve developer workflows and engineering metrics, automate repetitive operational work, and create scalable processes that allow teams to operate with greater autonomy, predictability, and transparency. This is a hands-on role for someone who is passionate about understanding how software organizations work and making them meaningfully better.

This position is considered hybrid, allowing for a combination of remote work and in-office collaboration. Qualified applicants must live within commuting distance of our Boston office location and should expect to be in office 3 days a week.

What You'll Do

Design, build, and continuously improve the processes, workflows, tools, and operating mechanisms used across the Sonos software development organization.
Help build an AI-enabled software development lifecycle, using AI agents, automation, APIs, and deterministic workflows to reduce manual work and make engineering processes easier to use.
Develop engineering metrics and feedback systems that help teams understand developer productivity, quality, flow, predictability, and organizational health.
Help define and operate the planning and execution mechanisms that allow multiple autonomous software teams and programs to work effectively within a shared development model.
Work directly with engineering teams to identify friction and bottlenecks, understand root causes, implement improvements, and measure outcomes.
Turn complex or manual organizational processes into scalable systems that teams can use without requiring constant coordination or facilitation.
Use data to evaluate the effectiveness of operational changes and communicate findings to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Contribute to the roadmapping, work tracking, and capacity planning systems that enable better investment and execution decisions.

Hands-on experience with software development tools such as Jira, Confluence, GitHub, CI/CD platforms, cloud services, or similar engineering systems.
Practical experience using AI tools in your work and an interest in applying AI and automation to engineering workflows.
Experience using data and metrics to understand problems, evaluate improvements, and drive decisions.
Ability to work effectively with engineers and technical leaders while communicating clearly across technical and non-technical audiences.

jobs.description:
About WPP Media

WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. With exceptional talent, trusted data and intelligence, and world-class partnerships – all united by our pioneering agentic marketing platform, WPP Open – we help clients navigate change, capture opportunity, and deliver transformational growth. 

WPP Media is WPP's AI-driven media operating unit, bringing together media, data, and partnerships to deliver creative personalisation at scale. Connected through WPP Open and powered by Open Intelligence, clients see exactly where, how, and why their media investment is working.

For more information, visit wppmedia.com.

PURPOSE

The purpose of this document is to help prospective team members better understand the role and responsibilities of the position of Solutions Project Manager at OpenDoor, WPP’s bespoke global operating model for Amazon. The role may also be referred to as Technical Project Manager.

About Wpp & Opendoor

At WPP, we’re constantly reinventing the future of creativity on an ever-broader canvas, bringing together unrivalled talent, resources and skills to provide an integrated offer of communications, experience, commerce and technology.

Over the last decade, we have developed a dedicated global client practice with the mission of accelerating WPP’s impact for our largest clients by bringing them the best of WPP. Each team is custom-built around a client’s specific needs and challenges, providing easy access to the right capabilities. And that’s why we’ve built OpenDoor
for Amazon
.

OpenDoor
is a unique integration of the best of WPP and Amazon – building on their respective strengths and visions. Whether at WPP or at Amazon, every project is an OpenDoor on new possibilities. Anything and everything can be an opportunity for our people to drive impact – for them to innovate, learn, thrive, and occasionally fail too.

The unique OpenDoor partnership model is built to deliver next level productivity, fuelled by our industry-leading approach to People, Platforms, and Process. OpenDoor spans across all WPP agencies and disciplines such as media, business consultancy, communications and brand strategy, tech and commerce, public relations, and production.

OpenDoor’s values are built from Amazon’s own 16 Leadership Principles, and WPP’s core values of Open, Optimistic and Extraordinary. Together, when WPP’s Creative Transformation meets Amazon’s next-level customer centricity, our people come together to challenge and impact what’s done today and build a better future.

By joining OpenDoor, not only are you joining a cross-function team partnering with one of WPP’s top five global clients, but you are also taking a step to challenge yourself and the world around you every day, working in the most unusual way on some of Earth’s most ambitious opportunities in marketing, tech, media, business, and creativity.

About The Role

We are looking for an experienced Solutions Project Manager to introduce the delivery rigour needed to turn complex Data and Technology requirements into clear, manageable and achievable plans. This role sits at the centre of OpenDoor’s advertising data and technology delivery environment, aligning dependencies, milestones, resources and decisions across Data Excellence, Data Engineering, Business Intelligence, Measurement, Product and wider technical partners.

This role is based in London and reports into the OpenDoor VP Excellence & Engineering (Solutions Architect) leadership team. It provides the structure through which OpenDoor manages client expectations and resource utilisation, maintains an integrated view of delivery, establishes clear ownership, identifies risks and constraints early, and ensures technical and non-technical stakeholders have accurate information on progress, decisions and next steps.

No two days are the same. This is a role where you will be challenged and have the platform to flex your delivery skills and make significant impact in a fast-paced, collaborative and high-impact team environment.

Responsibilities

Translate agreed solution scope into end-to-end delivery plans covering discovery, requirements, design, build, quality assurance, user acceptance, deployment, handover and closure.
Map and actively manage cross-discipline dependencies, critical paths, sequencing and hand-offs across Data and Technology teams and external partners.
Work with solution owners and discipline leads to confirm objectives, deliverables, acceptance criteria, assumptions and exclusions, maintaining traceability from requirements through to delivery and sign-off.
Establish proportionate governance, including project kick-offs, workstream plans, RAID management, decision logs, status reporting, change control, steering forums and escalation routes.
Partner with discipline leads to identify required skills, resource demand, availability and constraints, highlighting capacity conflicts early and supporting prioritisation decisions based on delivery impact.
Create clear, reliable communication structures for client and account stakeholders, including delivery milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions, changes and recovery plans.
Facilitate effective collaboration between data, engineering, BI, measurement, product, operations, market and client teams, ensuring actions have clear owners and completion dates.
Identify and assess risks and issues, drive mitigation and resolution, maintain escalation discipline, and evaluate the impact of requested changes on scope, timeline, quality and resource.
Coordinate quality assurance, user acceptance, documentation, training, access, support models and production-readiness checks before release or handover.
Provide concise, evidence-based reporting on milestones, forecast dates, delivery confidence, resource pressure, decisions required and corrective actions.
Review delivery performance and lessons learned, then improve templates, workflows and project controls to increase consistency, transparency and predictability across the Data and Technology portfolio.

Qualifications

Proven experience delivering complex technical, data or digital projects in a matrixed organisation, agency, consultancy or software environment.
A strong track record of building and managing integrated plans that span multiple technical disciplines, teams, markets or delivery partners.
Practical knowledge of Agile, Waterfall and hybrid delivery approaches, with the judgement to apply proportionate controls to different types of work.
Experience managing scope, milestones, dependencies, RAID logs, change control, governance forums, status reporting and delivery recovery plans.
Clear and confident communicator with strong stakeholder management and facilitation abilities, able to collaborate effectively with technical and non-technical colleagues across cross-functional account teams, markets and business functions.
Confidence working with technical specialists across data engineering, analytics, business intelligence, cloud platforms, software development, data governance or adjacent fields.

Description

Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity. The Amazon Leo Security team owns the security of product and operations end-to-end. We provide the necessary infrastructure and mechanisms to ensure the security of our satellite constellation and to protect the integrity and confidentiality of our customer data. Our team drives the research & development, deployment and operation of several mission-critical security systems and mechanisms. You will work in a start-up like environment, backed by Amazon’s infrastructure to bootstrap security mechanisms, and help instill the security culture in the organization.

Export Control Requirement

Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national.

Key job responsibilities

In This Role, You Will

Be proactive in removing roadblocks, fostering innovation, and managing multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced environment, driving continuous improvement and efficiency.
Create, optimize, and support cross-functional working groups and projects, fostering collaboration and synergy across departments to enhance security capabilities.
Manage tight deadlines with precision and drive results, exhibiting exceptional attention to detail and ensuring the successful completion of projects and initiatives.
Own the program lifecycle for large, complex security initiatives spanning multiple teams and VP organizations, including mission, vision, tenets, and roadmap contributions.
Partner with security engineers and senior technical leaders to perform program-level design reviews and risk assessments and ensure architectural choices appropriately balance short-term needs with long-term security posture.
Develop and maintain program mechanisms – including risk registers, review processes, and reporting structures – to ensure security risks are tracked, escalated, and remediated in partnership with risk owners.
Simplify and streamline cross-functional processes to increase selections velocity and reduce friction for solution teams.
Collect, analyze, and synthesize data from a variety of sources to create compelling written and verbal communications for Director and VP-level audiences, including Amazon 6-pagers and Monthly Program Reviews.
Build consensus among discordant views, escalate effectively, and ensure business and technical stakeholder needs are aligned across the program.

A day in the life

In this role you'll work with a team of engineers, managers, and TPMs. You'll help identify business security priorities, mechanisms to address the security of Leo's products and services, and will work with partners and builder teams to simplify risk mitigation.

You will influence the security strategy of partner teams to optimize security outcomes for our customers. You'll participate in hiring, development, training of team members. You'll own a part of the team outcome and will be encouraged to grow your ownership and role.

About The Team

Diverse Experiences Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?

At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

What We're Looking For

You thrive in ambiguity and create clarity for others. You have experience managing programs spanning distributed systems, security infrastructure, or compliance-driven initiatives. You understand security controls, vulnerability management, SAST and DAST scanning systems well enough to have informed technical conversations and spot opportunities early. You manage through influence, not authority. You work across organizations with different priorities and build alignment. You communicate crisply to senior leadership, distinguishing signal from noise. You build mechanisms that scale: dashboards, status cadences, escalation paths, and dependency trackers that outlast any individual program review.

Inclusive Team Culture

In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

5+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams experience
5+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing and executing/delivering product and technical roadmaps
Background in satellite operations, aerospace, or highly regulated environments (ITAR/EAR)

LAN/WAN, SD-WAN, firewall, load balancing, connectivity and network security upgrades.
–    Cloud:
migrations to AWS, Azure or GCP, hybrid cloud architecture, landing zones and cloud operations readiness.

•   Manage either a large, complex infrastructure program or a portfolio of smaller concurrent projects.

•   Apply ITIL-aligned processes and work closely with IT Service Management on change, release and transition to operations.
What You Need

•   10+ years of project management experience, with significant focus on enterprise IT infrastructure.
•   Hands-on experience leading projects across on-prem, data center, network, cloud and access management environments.
•   A proven track record leading large infrastructure projects or a portfolio of smaller ones.
•   Strong executive communication skills, with demonstrated experience managing up to senior technology and business leaders.

Role Expectations

•   Serve as the single point of accountability for delivery across assigned infrastructure projects or portfolio.

•   Keep executive stakeholders informed on status, risks and costs, and bring decisions to them early, with options.

•   Work onsite in San Ramon five days a week as the visible, day-to-day lead for project teams and stakeholders.
