jobs.title: Outreach Program Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are

For more than 130 years, The Salvation Army has served people in need in communities across Canada and Bermuda. Building on our roots as a world-wide Christian church, each year we help more than 2 million people, providing necessities such as food, clothing and shelter. In addition, we support people experiencing unemployment, addiction and family challenges. We continually adapt and innovate to meet emerging needs and live out our mission, vision and values of hope, service, dignity and stewardship. As a faith- and values-based organization, we hire and serve people of all backgrounds and walks of life - there is a place for everyone to belong here.

Mission Statement

The Salvation Army exists to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in the communities of our world.

Job Description

POSITION PURPOSE SUMMARY:

The Outreach Program Manager is responsible for leading and overseeing Outreach and Housing Programs, ensuring services are delivered effectively and in alignment with The Salvation Army's policies, standards, and mission. This front-line management role provides supervision and support to staff, oversees program operations and case management, manages or assists with client caseloads, and addresses complex client needs. The position works collaboratively with internal teams, community partners, and municipal stakeholders to ensure clients receive appropriate supports that promote stability and self-sufficiency. Additionally, the Program Manager contributes to program development, maintains service quality and documentation standards, and ensures resources are used efficiently to achieve positive client outcomes.

Accountabilities

General
Provide oversight and leadership to both the Housing First and Outreach programs, ensuring organizational and departmental objectives are consistently accomplished.
Provide guidance and support to Housing Workers and Outreach Worker regarding client needs, complex cases, service barriers, and appropriate interventions.
Assist staff in problem-solving complex or high-risk client situations and, when appropriate, meet directly with clients to address concerns, expectations, barriers, and possible solutions.
Ensure program staff are following departmental procedures, case management expectations, documentation requirements, and established service guidelines.
Meet and communicate with City representatives and other community partners regarding Housing services, client needs, programming expectations, service delivery, and emerging concerns.
Ensure confidentiality is maintained in accordance with The Salvation Army policy and applicable legislation regarding client records and statistical data.
Program
Lead and, where applicable, perform all aspects of the case management process, including intake, assessment, goal planning, referrals, transition, and follow-up.
Develop, plan, implement, and oversee relevant Housing, and Outreach programming in consultation with the Program Director.
Oversee case management services, ensuring staff complete appropriate assessments, service planning, documentation, applications, referrals, advocacy, and ongoing support based on clients’ identified needs.
Oversee housing support services, including housing searches, viewings, client preparation, housing placement, move-in, and transition for aftercare and continued support.
Oversee program and services, including Pathway of Hope, ongoing case management, community referrals, advocacy, aftercare, and supports aimed at promoting client stability and independence.
Conduct monthly case management meetings with Housing AND Outreach staff to review client progress, barriers, complex cases, service needs, and next steps.
Provide consultation and support to staff regarding complex client situations and assist with developing appropriate solutions and service plans, including direct client involvement when management support is required.
Participate in Restrictive Services meetings and forgiveness reviews to review client restrictions and determine appropriate next steps in accordance with established guidelines.
Monitor client behaviour, intervene in crisis situations, and provide emotional support and advocacy as required.
Develop and maintain working relationships with community service providers, housing providers, municipal partners, and other agencies to support effective service delivery and client access to resources.
Attend relevant Pathway of Hope, Housing, City, community partnership, program meetings, and training as required.
Administration
Ensure that all program client/case management files are properly maintained.
Effectively utilize computer management systems to record participant documentation while maintaining confidentiality and providing statistical reports.
Prepare and submit program reports, statistics and evaluations as requested in a timely, accurate and organized manner.
Record and document all major occurrences and send them to Program Director.
Represent the organization in a professional and engaging manner.
Always treat the property of The Salvation Army with due care and caution and act in the best interest of the employer.
Human Resources
Participate in hiring, orientation, training, and employee (Include internship student and volunteer) development, provide ongoing, consistent coaching, performance feedback, and manage employees’ performance evaluation.
Responsible for preparing, and maintaining departmental staff/student/volunteer schedules, approving employee time off (vacation, sick, etc. ...) time, and submitting time sheets to the Administrative Coordinator.
Ensure that all employees/student/volunteer have completed the required mandatory training and is up to date; identify staff training needs to the Program Director.
In consultation with Program Director complete and update position descriptions and job duties for those supervised.
Identify job vacancies and follow The Salvation Army Windsor Centre of Hope hiring procedures.
Understand and comply with Union Collective Agreement.
Health and Safety
Responsible for maintaining a level of competency and understand Sections 25 and 26 of the Occupational Health and Safety Act (OHSA).
Ensure that the measures and procedures prescribed (OH&SA) are carried out in the workplace and that every reasonable precaution is taken for the protection of the worker and workplace.
Provide advice, make recommendations and improvements, and assist with the development of company policies/guidelines/handbooks as it relates to health and safety.
Work in compliance with OH&S Act and Regulations and abide by The Salvation Army’s health and safety policies and procedures.
Finance
Monitoring the program expenditures. Responsible for effective and efficient management of all financial resources of the organization. Maintain a balanced budget.

Internal

CRITICAL RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT:

Program Director, management members, staff, volunteers, and residents.
Conduct regular staff meetings to review operational effectiveness, changes in policies and procedures, and to provide in-service training.
Participate in management meeting and other staff meetings when relevant.

External

Community partners and community members who receive our services.
Attend approved community meetings. {Required to use the program vehicle when available}

Managerial/Technical Responsibilities

This position reports directly to the Program Director or designate.
The incumbent is responsible for the direct supervision of non-supervisory personnel, and has input into discipline, hiring, or firing decisions within the established guidelines.

Financial And Material Management

Not applicable

Working Conditions

This is a permanent full-time position.
This position is considered a management position for the purposes of the Employment Standards Act of Ontario and as such is not covered by various ESA rules, including but not limited to those related to hours of work, daily and weekly rest periods and overtime compensation. Salary is based on average minimum weekly hours of 40 per week and hours worked are compensated through the annual salary amount.
May be required to work weekends to support the Centre operation.
Working environment is typically in the office in generally agreeable conditions.
Travel is associated with this position {5%}. i.e., to attend community partnership meetings or visit program participants.

Education And Expereince Requirements

Minimum of an undergraduate university degree in Social Work, Human Services, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. A master’s degree in social work or a related discipline is preferred.
Valid Ontario Class “G” Driver’s License, current copy of driver’s abstract that is satisfactory to The Salvation Army, in its sole discretion, is required.
Must provide an original copy of a Background Check with vulnerable sector screening that is satisfactory to The Salvation Army, in its sole discretion, is required. The screening is secured either through the national Canadian Police Information Centre (CPIC) or through a local police detachment.
Current First Aid and CPR certificate, Non-Violent Crisis Intervention training, WHIMS certificate.

Skills And Capabilities

Able to work independently and participate as an active and responsible team member.
Strong sense of integrity and confidentiality with professional ethics and a balanced sense of fairness and flexibility.
Committed to service excellence, inspires, and motivates teams to reach their full potential.
Knowledge of community-based resources is required and experience networking with community service agencies.
Ability to organize and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
Strong interpersonal, motivational, leadership, and organizational skills.
Ability to develop and maintain a team environment; work cooperatively and effectively with others to set goals, resolve problems, and make decisions that enhance organizational effectiveness.
Strong oral/written communication skills.
Self-motivated/disciplined.
Attention to detail, problem solving and analytical skills.
Attentive listening skills for the purpose of supervision, coaching, and conflict resolution.

Compensation

The target hiring range for this position is $55,244.80 to $69,076.80 with a maximum of $82,888.00.

Placement in the salary range will be based on factors such as market conditions, internal equity, and candidate experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the role.

The Salvation Army will provide reasonable accommodation upon request. Please email Recruitment.Accommodations@salvationarmy.ca
if you have a need for any accommodation and we will be pleased to discuss this with you.

The Statewide Residency Training Program is seeking a Program Manager to manage and direct the Iowa Health Professions Inventory (Iowa HPINV) and related services through planning, promotion, and implementation. The Iowa HPINV has a specific set of unique goals and objectives that complement the three core missions of the University: teaching, research, and service. The Program Manager position assumes responsibility for developing and administering all program elements of the Iowa HPINV which includes a minimum of a twice annual update of the entire active workforce for all physicians (~5800), physician assistants (~1300), advance practice nurses (~3900), pharmacists (~3000), and dentists (~1500) for a total of over 15,000 active providers in Iowa to be managed (plus maintain archived health professionals with thousands more dating back to 1977), analyzed and reported upon. The Program Director leads strategic planning initiatives and is responsible for all aspects of this large, complex, and valued resource for the state of Iowa. Manage implementation and maintenance of CME learning management system, including training new employees on use of system as needed.

Oversee the development of report formats, data products, and price schedules for report requests from the University of Iowa and non-University clients.

Develop strategies for budget priorities.

jobs.description:
Dallas is Growing. Grow With Us.

Looking for more than just a job? The City of Dallas offers careers with purpose. With competitive benefits, growth opportunities, and a vibrant work culture,

we’re committed to helping you thrive while you help our city flourish. Be part of a team that’s committed to service, innovation, and community.

Job Summary

Performs operational intelligence analysis work by providing direct, critical, front-line intelligence support toongoing crime investigations for all levels of Police Officers, Managers and Executives.

Overview

Job Description

The Senior Criminal Intelligence Analyst performs operational intelligence analysis work by providing direct, critical, front-line intelligence support to ongoing crime investigations for all levels of Police Officers, Managers, and Executives.

Essential Functions

1
Prepares graphs, charts, tables, matrices, maps, and other illustrative devices for analysis and visual presentation of data related to a current, ongoing, or continuing investigation or project.

2
Collects, collates, analyzes, and disseminates information concerning criminal activity currently under investigation, including the analysis of specific datasets to identify specific persons for further investigation.

3
Identifies gaps in existing criminal investigative data and prepares comprehensive written reports that accurately reflect all information gathered and analyzed in the course of an investigation.

4
Obtains and analyzes information and gathers facts by participating in debriefings of informants, witnesses, and others with information about criminal activity.

5
Works directly with and makes suggestions and recommendations to case Police Officers and Detectives on investigative strategies and direction that may be productive.

6
Makes assignments and delegates tasks to other analysts, investigators, and agents to aid in the coordinated effort of other law enforcement personnel during major criminal investigations.

7
Prepares and disseminates reports and relevant information to appropriate information consumers to assist in coordinating and directing intelligence, investigative, enforcement, and prevention activities performed by the Department and other agencies.

8
Attends intelligence, investigation, and law enforcement information sharing meetings; researches records and uses computerized databases to conduct investigations, usually based on specific requests for information or in response to identifiable events.

9
Prepares and disseminates reports and relevant information to the appropriate information consumers to assist in furthering intelligence, investigative, enforcement and prevention activities performed by the Department and other agencies.

10
May present testimony at preliminary hearings, grand jury proceedings, and trials regarding investigations conducted by the Department; performs briefings to present intelligence data to authorized officials.

11
Performs any and all other work as needed or assigned.

Knowledge And Skills

1
Knowledge of the functions and organization of local, state, and federal government; of law enforcement operations and procedures; and, department safety policies, methods, and procedures.

2
Knowledge of various sources of data, methods of obtaining data and techniques used in the analysis of data.

3
Knowledge of computers and related systems to develop computer programs for data collection and analysis purposes

4
Knowledge of important local, national, and international events that may have an impact on a given program area or investigation; knowledge of the intelligence cycle, and intelligence and analytic methods.

5
Knowledge of principles, techniques, current trends, laws, policies, and programs concerning the application of intelligence to all phases of local, state, and federal investigations, and planning and development.

6
Ability to plan and organize assigned work priorities and to handle a variety of assignments.

7
Ability to correctly interpret state and federal programs, legislation, policies, and procedures.

8
Ability to recall pertinent facts obtained in research of criminal investigation data and to critically evaluate information from multiple sources and determine the importance and limitations of each piece of information.

9
Ability to draw inferences and apply inductive and deductive logic in the analysis of criminal activities.

10
Ability to efficiently operate computer equipment, including word processing, spreadsheet, data base, and graphics software, visualization tools, and other analytical programs.

11
Ability to conduct intelligence analysis and prepare investigative reports and analytical charts or graphs which may display patterns, events, identities or activities of criminal groups and individuals.

12
Ability to explain and demonstrate various aspects of the job and serve as a positive role model to other employees.

13
Communicating effectively verbally and in writing.

14
Establishing and maintaining effective working relationships.

Education

Minimum Qualifications

High school diploma or GED

Experience

Four (4) years of experience as a crime analyst or intelligence analyst working for a local, state or federal law enforcement agency.

Equivalancies

An associate degree (or higher) in a non-specified field plus two (2) years of the required experience will meet the education and experience requirements.
Bachelor's degree in a criminal justice, forensic science, terrorism/counterterrorism, cyber security, information technology, geographic science, political science, emergency management or related field plus one (1) year of the required experience will meet the education and experience requirements.
A master's degree (or higher) in a specified field will meet the education and experience requirements.

LICENSE And/or CERTIFICATION

Valid driver's license with good driving record.

Other Requirements

Must pass an intensive background investigation and drug test.
No felony or class A misdemeanor convictions.
No class B misdemeanor convictions in the last ten (10) years.
No family violence convictions.
Cannot currently be on deferred adjudication for any felony, class A or class B misdemeanor.
Availability for varying shifts, nights/weekends/holidays

Preferences

Knowledge of principles and techniques of crime analysis and/or data analysis.
MS Office or similar software skills
Ability to conduct statistical analysis using computer and applicable software.
Ability to collect, analyze, interpret, and effectively report any intelligence obtained from the analysis.
Experience as a Fusion Center analyst
Experience as a Real Time Crime Center analyst
Previous experience as an analyst within a Law Enforcement Organization
Communications/Dispatch experience
Bachelor's Degree and/or higher education in related fields such as but not limited to criminal justice, forensic science, emergency management.
Prior analytical and/or training working knowledge with law enforcement computer systems/programs and/or databases
Currently working as a Law Enforcement Criminal Intelligence Analyst
Multi lingual
Ability to have or obtain a secret level security clearance from the Department of Homeland Security is preferred.

$27.45 - $32.58

jobs.title: Vendor Threat Mitigation Program Analyst - TS/SCI Clearance
jobs.description:
Join our Deloitte AI & Engineering team to transform technology platforms, drive innovation, and help make a significant impact on our clients' success. You'll work alongside talented professionals reimagining and reengineering operations and processes that are critical to businesses. Your contributions can help clients improve financial performance, accelerate new digital ventures, and fuel growth through innovation.

Work You'll Do

As a Project Lead Integration Engineer II on the project, provide critical Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) and Vendor Threat Mitigation (VTM) planning, coordination, and intelligence-integration. The role ensures the security and resilience of the theater supply chain by identifying, assessing, and mitigating vendor-related risks-including foreign ownership, control, or influence (FOCI), cyber vulnerabilities, and adversarial exploitation-across the Area of Responsibility (AOR). The role is highly dynamic and adaptive to command priorities; requiring an experienced professional who can operate independently with minimal guidance.

The VTM Program Analyst serves as a key contractor supporting Geographic Combatant Command (GCC) secure logistics objectives. The role focuses on the strategic planning of vendor threat assessments and supply chain illumination, aligned with the Theater Campaign Plan, Posture Plan, and Department of Defense (DoD) SCRM directives. A primary requirement is the ability to conduct high-level risk framework analysis and all-source intelligence reports, integrate them for mitigation actions into major joint operations, exercise support, and coalition logistics. As required, forward adversarial findings and reports to respective procurement contracting agencies and associated authorities to take direct action against vendor threats. Exceptional written and oral communication skills, with the ability to successfully collaborate in multi-echelon Joint Logistics and Intelligence Enterprises (JLEnt/JIE), are mandatory for success in this role.

Key Responsibilities:

Threat Analysis & Illumination: Conduct rigorous supply chain illuminations and vendor threat assessments to identify FOCI, cyber vulnerabilities, and adversarial influence risks within the AOR, ensuring mission requirements are protected from compromised suppliers
Mitigation Planning: Develop and implement theater-specific VTM mitigation strategies and risk response plans, ensuring alignment with DoD security protocols and mission-critical function protection
Exercise & Operation Integration: Support VTM planning for Tier 1 and Tier 2 Exercises (e.g., Balikatan, Cobra Gold), ensuring theater supply chains are modeled, stress-tested against subversion, and assessed during major training events
Interagency & Partner Sync: Synchronize vendor threat intelligence and mitigation strategies with USFK, USFJ, SOCPAC, and regional Service Components. Coordinate with DCSA, DLA, and USTRANSCOM to ensure a unified theater defense
Governance & Reporting: Serve as a subject matter expert for VTM policy and governance. Draft formal staff products (EXSUMs, Info Papers) and deliver executive-level briefings to General/Flag Officers (GO/FO) regarding theater supply chain vulnerabilities.
Doctrine & Planning Proficiency: Deeply understand and apply the following Joint Publications (JPs), DoD Directives and Instructions (DoDD/DoDI), and associated policies that support theater distribution security and vendor threat mitigation:
DoDD 5000.01, The Defense Acquisition System: Mandates supply chain risk management, security, and resilience throughout the acquisition lifecycle and sustainment operations.
DoDD 5240.02, Counterintelligence (CI): Establishes foundational CI policy essential for identifying and mitigating foreign intelligence threats, FOCI, and espionage within the vendor base.
DoDI 5200.44: Protection of Mission Critical Functions to Achieve Trusted Systems and Networks (TSN).
DoDI 4140.01: DoD Supply Chain Materiel Management Policy (with focus on SCRM and resilience).
DoDI 5000.90: Cybersecurity for Acquisition Decision Authorities and Program Managers.
JP 4-0 / JP 4-01: Joint Logistics and the Joint Deployment and Distribution Enterprise (JDDE).
JP 4-10, Operational Contract Support (OCS): Integration of commercial support into joint operations, including the assessment of vendor-related risks to force protection and mission assurance.
JP 2-0 / JP 3-0: Joint Intelligence and Joint Operations integration for threat-informed logistics.
NDAA Compliance: Specific expertise in Sections 889 (telecommunications) and 5949 (semiconductors) prohibitions within theater of operations.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
Effective written and verbal communication skills
Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
Ability to lead projects or workstreams
Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
Ability to meet deadlines
Ability to provide clear guidance to others

The Team

Deloitte's Government & Public Services (GPS) practice - our people, ideas, technology and outcomes - is designed for impact. Serving federal, state, & local government clients as well as public higher education institutions, our team of professionals brings fresh perspective to help clients anticipate disruption, reimagine the possible, and fulfill their mission promise.

Our Industry Solutions clients seek verticalized solutions that transform how they sell products, deliver services, generate growth, and fulfill mission-critical operations. The Industry Solutions offering delivers integrated business expertise with repeatable scaled technology solutions that are specifically engineered for each sector's IndustryAdvantageTM.

The Project Delivery Talent Model is designed for professionals with specialized skills that align to a current client need. Team members focus on delivering services to clients, without additional expectations related to business development or promotion. Their employment is tied to their role on a project, and they are eligible for a benefits package that is competitive for project delivery-focused professionals.

Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor's Degree in a related field
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future
Active TS SCI security clearance required
5+ years of GCC & Component experience, operating within a GCC logistics, operations, or intelligence environment (e.g., J4, J2, or J3) or at a sub-unified/Service Component level.
5+ years of SCRM & VTM experience, including theater-level supply chain risk management, open-source intelligence (OSINT) research, and experience integrating VTM requirements into the Joint Exercise Life Cycle (JELC).
5+ years of systems experience, including supply chain platforms or similar DoD-approved tools and contracting databases (e.g. GCSS, IGC and EBS)
5+ years of experience in DoD contracting and acquisition systems (e.g., Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE), SAM.gov, CPARS, or Procurement Desktop-Defense (PD2)) to support vendor vetting.
Able to travel occasionally, no more than four times a year

The Research Security Analyst supports the development and implementation of a comprehensive and integrated research security program designed to protect critical research, secure the academic environment from undue foreign influence, and support compliance with federal and state research security requirements. jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Apprentify Group is a portfolio of six specialist companies, each with its own culture, personality and people. Together, we support more than 10,000 learners a year and work with 200+ employers across the UK across data, tech, AI, leadership, sales and digital marketing.

As an Ofsted Outstanding provider and a specialist in AI, data and tech apprenticeships, we're growing quickly and becoming increasingly data-led in how we make decisions.

We need a Data Analyst
ready to turn complex data into clear insight, building the reporting, dashboards and analysis that help our board, senior leadership and teams understand how the business is performing and make better commercial decisions.

THE QUICK FACTS

Location:
Wilmslow office initially, moving to hybrid once settled

Contract:
Full-time, permanent

Salary:
£30,000–£32,000 depending on experience

Start:
Immediate or near-term

Reports to:
Project Director

Level:
Junior to mid-level, we're hiring for potential

LIFE IN THE ROLE

The real work:
Most of your time will be spent building and maintaining dashboards and management reporting, analysing operational and commercial KPIs, bringing together data from different systems and turning numbers into insight that people across the group can actually use.

You'll work with data from areas including learner management systems, HubSpot, finance platforms such as Xero, sales and operations. You'll also write and maintain SQL queries, investigate data quality issues and help create a single, reliable view of performance across the group.

You'll also work directly with teams across sales, product, operations, marketing and finance, translating loosely defined questions into clear analysis and presenting your findings to senior, non-technical audiences.

This is a role where your work will be visible. Your reporting will support board and senior leadership discussions, major enterprise accounts and group-wide growth initiatives.

The environment:
You'll be based in our Wilmslow office initially. That's deliberate getting to know the business, our people and how our data fits together is an important part of the role. Once you're established and settled, we'll agree a hybrid working pattern together.

You won't be handed a perfect specification every time. Requests may come from several stakeholders at once, sometimes as a fairly messy brief. You'll need to ask the right questions, work out what's actually needed and take ownership of getting to a useful answer.

TEAM & CULTURE

You'll join a central, group-wide function
, working closely with sales, product, operations, marketing and finance across our different brands.

How we work:
Clear expectations, genuine ownership of how you deliver against them. You'll have the opportunity to shape how we report, measure and understand performance rather than simply maintaining existing reports.

THE HONEST HARD BIT

The data won't always be clean and the questions won't always be neatly packaged.

You may have several stakeholders asking for different things at the same time, data coming from different systems that doesn't immediately align, or a request where the answer isn't obvious from the outset.

You'll need to be comfortable investigating what's behind the numbers, challenging something when it doesn't add up and explaining what you've found clearly even when the answer isn't necessarily what someone wanted to hear.

It's a growing business, so processes and reporting structures will continue to evolve. This role suits someone who sees that as an opportunity to build, improve and learn.

IS THIS FOR YOU?

✔ You enjoy turning data into clear, practical business insight

✔ You naturally question whether the numbers are accurate before presenting them

✔ You're comfortable working with SQL, Excel and a BI/reporting tool such as Power BI

✔ You can explain analysis clearly to people who aren't data specialists

✔ You're curious enough to challenge a brief or a figure when something doesn't add up

✔ You're comfortable operating in a scale-up environment, ambiguity included

This is NOT for you if:

✘ You need every task to come with a detailed step-by-step specification

✘ You prefer working with one clean dataset rather than investigating how different data sources connect

✘ You'd rather produce reports than understand what the numbers actually mean

✘ You're uncomfortable questioning data, assumptions or requests from stakeholders

✘ You need a fully structured corporate environment to do your best work

What You Bring

Experience in a Data, MI or BI role, ideally producing reporting for managers or senior stakeholders
Practical experience using SQL and an understanding of relational data
Experience building reports or dashboards using Power BI, Excel or a similar tool
Experience bringing together data from more than one source, such as CRM, finance or operational systems
Understanding of KPIs, performance measurement and business reporting
Excellent attention to detail and a genuine focus on data quality
Strong organisation skills and the ability to manage competing requests and deadlines
Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain analysis simply to non-technical audiences
Curiosity and confidence to challenge a brief, question a figure and investigate when something doesn't look right

Nice to have:

Experience with DAX or data modelling in Power BI
Familiarity with HubSpot, Xero or apprenticeship/learner management systems
Exposure to Microsoft Azure or other cloud data platforms
Experience with Python, Power Automate or data automation
Experience in education, training or the skills sector
An interest in AI and how it's changing the way organisations work

WHAT WE OFFER

25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays), increasing with length of service
Birthday Leave + Volunteer Day
Private medical insurance
Hybrid working once established in the role, with regular collaboration at our Wilmslow HQ
Ongoing professional development and leadership support
Opportunity to join one of our own Data or AI apprenticeship programmes following successful probation
Structured CPD support
Enhanced family leave policies
Access to mental health and wellbeing support
Benefits portal with access to 700+ deals
Regular company-wide events and team socials

THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

Recruiter call:

An introductory 30-minute call with the Talent team to discuss the role, your experience, motivation, salary expectations, notice period, right to work and the initial office-based requirement.

Stage 1 interview – Data review & interview:

You'll complete a short data exercise in advance and present your findings during an 80-minute in-person interview in Wilmslow. We'll explore how you approach data, identify insights, assess data quality and turn your analysis into practical recommendations.

Final interview (45–60 minutes):

A final in-person conversation focused on commercial judgement, communication, stakeholder management, trust and your longer-term development within the role.

Please note:
The postholder will be required to undergo Safer Recruitment check prior to starting work, including an appropriate level of DBS check (dependent on role) and a reference check.

We welcome and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, particularly those who are currently underrepresented in our workforce. We value different perspectives, lived experiences and ways of thinking and we recognise the positive impact they have on our learners, our culture and our organisation.

We are dedicated to removing barriers in our recruitment process and will provide reasonable adjustments where needed to ensure all candidates have a fair opportunity to succeed.

If you have any questions about the application process or would like to discuss reasonable adjustments, please get in touch with us – we’re here to support you.

Utilize technical expertise, analytical problem-solving skills, and operational judgment to address evolving cybersecurity challenges.

Experience providing operational updates, threat briefings, executive reporting, and recommendations to senior leaders.

jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager, Amazon LATAM Payments Trust
jobs.description:
Description

Lead the fight against fraud and abuse across Amazon's Payments business in Latam. As Senior Program Manager for Payment Integrity, you'll own the strategy, roadmap, and team that protect millions of customers — and the business — from fraud, abuse, and bad debt across BR and LATAM.

You will act as the single-threaded owner for payment integrity in the region, leading a team of program and product managers and owning an ambitious Cost of Business Waste (CoBW) reduction target. You'll stay ahead of a fast-moving fraud and abuse landscape, translate it into a clear multi-year roadmap, extend proven prevention mechanisms to new financial products such as Amazon Credito, and partner deeply with engineering, risk, compliance, and finance teams. If you are energized by ambiguous, high-stakes problems where the mechanisms you build directly protect customers and the business, this role is for you.

Key job responsibilities

Lead the Integrity / F&AP team: guide, coordinate and develop a team of program and product managers, set priorities, and own the operational drumbeat, incident response, and delivery bar for the pillar.
Stay ahead of the fraud & abuse landscape — maintain deep, current knowledge of market solutions, industry mechanisms, and emerging fraud/abuse vectors (card fraud, concession/promo abuse, instrument and credential abuse), and bring that outside-in view into our roadmap.
Define the strategy and roadmap — own the multi-year vision and prioritized roadmap for payment integrity across BR and LATAM, including fraud & abuse coverage for new products (e.g., Amazon Credito) and the extension of proven mechanisms across markets.
Drive and track projects and metrics — oversee execution of in-flight initiatives (abuse-reduction programs, card-related and bad-debt initiatives), own the LATAM CoBW reduction target, and hold the team accountable to measurable input and output metrics.
Report status to leadership — provide clear, data-driven updates on roadmap progress, CoBW performance, risks, and trade-offs to senior leadership through the established review cadence (MBR/QBR/OP).
Partner cross-org — align and influence across engineering, RCS, BRP, BAP, Risk, Compliance, and Finance to unblock delivery and scale prevention mechanisms.

A day in the life

No two days look the same. You might start by reviewing the latest fraud metrics with your team, deciding where to double down and where to cut losses. Mid-morning, you pressure-test the design of a new abuse-prevention mechanism with engineering before it goes to build. In the afternoon, you align with Product and Risk on how a new product launch changes our fraud exposure and what coverage we need . You close by refining the roadmap and preparing a crisp update for leadership on progress against our CoBW target — moving fluidly between deep strategy and hands-on execution.

About The Team

Amazon LATAM Payments Trust builds the compliance, identity, and fraud & abuse prevention mechanisms that create trust in payment transactions — letting millions of customers transact safely and enabling Amazon to scale new products in a dynamic payments markets. We own this end-to-end across the region, from setting strategy to shipping the mechanisms that run in production.

We are a small, senior, high-trust team with a lot of ownership and a strong bias for action. We think in mechanisms, not one-offs; we ground decisions in data; and we care about building things that last and replicate across markets.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree
Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
Driving process improvements experience

Description

At Amazon, we're looking for a Sr. Program Manager for Amazon Flex. Amazon Flex works directly with independent contractors – called delivery partners – to make deliveries to our customers. With Amazon Flex, individuals can now be their own boss delivering Amazon packages. Amazon Flex is powered by a mobile app that works in concert with our advanced logistics systems that allows delivery partners to on-board, schedule delivery times, guide them through their deliveries with in-app mapping and navigation, and more.

The Sr. Program Manager will own the design and execution of evaluation and enforcement frameworks for delivery partners at scale. You will build mechanisms that prevent defects across station and on-road operations — identifying root causes, fixing underlying process failures, and ensuring recurrence does not happen. This includes continuous improvement of how delivery partners receive guidance, how delivery history is surfaced, and how corrective actions are applied consistently across the network.

This role requires troubleshooting, root cause identification, problem-solving, analytical reasoning, and the ability to operate in a fast-paced environment. You will partner cross-functionally with Operations, Legal, and senior leadership (Directors and VPs) to drive technology enhancements, process redesign, policy recalibration, and enforcement governance.

Key job responsibilities

Manage the full lifecycle of complex cross-functional programs with considerable impact across multiple organizations, developing overall program strategy and tactically driving teams inside and outside your organization to deliver results
Establish and maintain scalable mechanisms for Service Level Standards (SLS) evaluation processes, including reporting systems, quality metrics, and mitigation processes that maintain program quality and exceptional customer experiences
Analyze defect data from multiple sources to identify patterns, uncover root causes, and implement mitigation programs that reduce repeat defect rates
Define program mission, vision, and tenets; set objectives; and drive improvements that are quantified with metrics
Partner with customers and cross-functional stakeholders to determine project priorities, allocate resources, and resolve ambiguous problems — proactively identifying and mitigating risks before they become roadblocks
Oversee gaps between teams, processes, and systems; reduce exposure to classic failure modes
Write and present effective narratives to Directors and VPs, manage executive escalations, and drive consensus across diverse teams
Work autonomously in an ambiguous environment, seeking to understand business problems, automation limitations, and process enhancement requirements

A day in the life

Your day revolves around analyzing delivery defect data trends and working across teams to improve quality outcomes. You'll dive into defect patterns across Under-the-Roof, On-the-Road, Customer Doorstep, and Return to Station touchpoints, collaborating with Operations and tech teams to understand issues. You'll spend time building dashboards and reporting mechanisms, responding to escalations, and meeting with cross-functional partners including Legal and senior leadership to align on enforcement strategies. You'll also dedicate time to ensuring solutions scale effectively across geographies and business lines.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements

Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
Knowledge of general AI tools
Experience designing, implementing, and scaling upskilling, apprenticeship, or workforce development programs across large-scale operations or corporate environments, including forecasting workforce needs and leveraging analytics to drive program decisions

jobs.description:
Description

Business Analyst in Network Strategy and Performance owns processes & analytics that directly shape how Amazon serves customers globally. They are an analytical problem solver who is comfortable in a fast-paced, multi-tasked, high-energy environment. They are self-motivated, operating independently in an autonomous environment to deliver an exceptional customer experience with little to no guidance. They operationalize the long- and short-term staffing plans, working cross-functionally with site Operations, planning teams, training, finance, and others. They will contribute to the team's AI-driven transformation agenda by applying AI tools to increase the speed, quality, and scale of analytical outputs. They do not just report or fix defects, but think critically about why they happen, what surrounds them, and how to prevent them — combining analytical rigor with a proactive, anticipatory mindset.

Key job responsibilities

Create and accurately maintain CSA shift schedules ensuring shifts are optimally planned to meet the sites short term forecast requirements and Service Levels (SL).
Monitor actual staffing levels against planned staffing and take the relevant corrective actions as required improve SL.
Effectively plan and monitor CSA adherence to assigned schedule, including productive and non-productive activities.
Work closely with mid to senior-level leaders across core teams to identify and mitigate emerging risks and assists in creating mitigation plans for staffing corrections and SL recovery.
Responsible for coordinating site-staffing needs including reporting and analysis of site headcount numbers as per staffing plan.
Understanding and monitor symptoms of CSA burnout, detecting the metrics that can signal these symptoms and assist in implementing interventions to eliminate outlier experiences.
Responsible to coordinate various cross-training, new-hires, and management of network and site-wide shift rotation processes as per business need.
Create work schedules for associates, identifies and proactively resolves headcount deficiencies and overages.
Investigate defects and operational anomalies to identify systemic drivers (system-related, behavioral, or shared responsibility), not just symptoms. Highlight and communicate metrics impacting the operation that could impact service levels, customer experience, and business process.
Build and maintain validation checks, dashboards, and automated alerts to catch defects early — before they impact customers or operations.
Independently apply AI tools (e.g., Amazon Q, generative AI assistants, AgentZ) to accelerate analytical workflows, identifying opportunities to improve speed and quality of outputs.
Apply AI tools to develop automation for repetitive tasks within your workstream, demonstrating measurable productivity improvement.

About The Team

The Network Strategy and Performance (NP) team defines and delivers the right human-assisted support to Amazon customers under demand and labor supply volatility, by optimizing the Amazon Customer Service (CS) network for customer experience, associate experience, and cost. We are responsible for: (1) planning customer support staffing; (2) preserving the customer experience when customers contact Customer Service; and (3) ensuring best costs for providing customer support.

We analyse historical data and anticipate potential business events to accurately predict the number of Customer Service Associates (CSAs) required for a given period. Our areas of expertise span forecasting, planning, optimization, data analytics, and reporting. We deliver our vision using operations research, data science, and program management — and we continue to challenge the status quo, invent and simplify, and deliver excellence for our customers.

The Network Performance team is on a transformation journey. We are building a future-ready team that combines analytical rigor with AI fluency, executive-level communication, and the ability to drive outcomes across organizational boundaries. We are seeking a Business Analyst to join this team and help shape how Amazon plans, staff, and optimizes its Customer Service network.

Basic Qualifications

1+ years of tax, finance or a related analytical field experience
2+ years of complex Excel VBA macros writing experience
Bachelor's degree or equivalent
Experience defining requirements and using data and metrics to draw business insights
Experience with SQL or ETL

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with Tableau
Experience using very large datasets

jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Global Corporate Communications (GCC) is looking for a Senior Program Manager to lead the data and AI systems that GCC's teams rely on. You'll build the shared foundation beneath GCC's work: making its data usable by AI, delivering the AI systems on top of it, and connecting the work across GCC and its partners.

Today, a lot of GCC's most valuable data is scattered. Research, media coverage, agency reporting, processes, and planning documents live in different places and formats, with different access. That makes it hard for teams to bring it together, and hard for AI to do anything with it. You'll connect those sources, structure them so AI can actually retrieve and reason over the content, and design tools on top of them. The teams who produce the data still own it. You make sure it's structured, accessible, and fits together, so everyone gets more out of it.

A lot of this job comes down to giving people across the team more ownership of their work. That happens two ways. First, by reducing dependencies, the places where people are stuck waiting on a manual step, a handoff, or the one person who knows how something works. Second, by clearing away the rote, repetitive work that fills their days. You'll get to know how GCC operates, find where both of these slow people down, and build what it takes to help. Everyone here is a builder, and your job is to support that.

No two months in this role look the same. The data keeps growing, the tools keep changing, and there's always a new challenge worth taking on. It's a great fit for someone who likes to work independently, dig into complex problems, and see their work make a difference across a team.

Job Description

The Manufacturing Project Manager is responsible for coordinating and tracking the key initiatives required to scale Harris’ manufacturing and supply chain capabilities. This role functions as a central portfolio management resource, helping leadership maintain visibility, accountability, and progress across multiple workstreams, including facility startups, manufacturing modifications, fulfillment center setup, process improvements, data integration, purchasing forecasting, and fabrication estimating.

As production scales, this role will also help convert manufacturing opportunities into actionable production plans by coordinating the handoff from business development, estimating, engineering, purchasing, and manufacturing operations.

This role does not own the technical solution, manufacturing operations, or supply chain functions, but ensures the right work is being planned, tracked, coordinated, and completed. This role serves as the coordination and accountability function for manufacturing and supply chain scale-up initiatives while ensuring opportunities transition effectively into production execution.

Core Responsibilities

Portfolio and Program Management

Help translate strategic initiatives into actionable plans with defined owners, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
Maintain portfolio-level visibility across manufacturing and supply chain initiatives, including facility setup, process improvement, systems, and operational readiness workstreams.
Develop/manage integrated project plans, milestones, activities, risks, and executive summaries.

Coordinate with manufacturing leadership, plant managers, industrial engineering, purchasing, facilities, and other stakeholders to maintain progress.

Cross-Functional Coordination and Accountability

Facilitate recurring coordination meetings across manufacturing, supply chain, engineering, estimating, business development, and operations.
Hold teams accountable to committed actions, milestones, and deliverables.
Identify interdependencies across workstreams and help resolve or escalate conflicts.

Reporting, Metrics & Communication

Develop clear reporting for initiative status, milestones, risks, blockers, and upcoming decisions.
Support dashboard development and data visibility efforts in partnership with BI teams.
Communicate progress in a concise, leadership-ready format.

Cross‑Functional Collaboration

Division and Business Unit Leadership
Manufacturing Business Development & Estimating
Manufacturing & Supply Chain Operations
Construction & Service/Building Automation Operations, where applicable
Industrial Engineering & Product Engineering
Facilities / Real Estate
Technology and Data teams

Required Qualifications

Experience managing cross-functional programs, projects, or operational initiatives.
Strong project management discipline, including schedules, milestones, action tracking, risk management, and executive reporting.

Strong communication skills with the ability to simplify complex moving parts into clear status, issues, and decisions.
Comfortable working in an environment where processes, systems, and roles are evolving.
Ability to influence, coordinate, and drive execution across multiple functions without direct authority.
Proficiency with project management tools, dashboards, spreadsheets, and reporting systems.

The coordination and accountability engine for manufacturing and supply chain initiatives.
A role supporting leadership across sales, facilities, systems, processes, and production.

A technology project manager.

Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

5+ years of experience in business operations, strategy, chief of staff roles, or technical program management, including direct support of senior leaders.

Proven experience managing operational tech stacks, vendor relationships, and tracking organizational budgets/OPEX or business cases.

Demonstrated ability to write and speak at a leadership altitude, holding the room and influencing cross-functional stakeholders without formal direct authority.

Exceptional ability to manage multiple complex threads, ensuring nothing is dropped, everything is documented, and decisions result in action.

Familiarity with cloud concepts (e.g., GCP, AWS, or Azure), cybersecurity, technical lab environments, or developer platforms.

Experience working inside or directly partnering with technical enablement, customer engineering, sales engineering, or customer success organizations.

About the Job:

As the Strategy & Operations Program Manager for Global Technical Enablement (GTE), you will serve as the operational right hand and proxy to the Head of GTE. This is not a general program-management role; your mandate is to build the operating system that runs the organization and keep the business inspection-ready at all times.

You will not have direct reports; instead, your influence and operational rigor will ensure that critical multi-team programs move smoothly from ideation to delivery. You will sit with the Head, be in the room for the decisions, carry their proxy, and govern the organization's technological, financial, and strategic resources. Ultimately, you will own the living story of the business, the cadence, the data narrative, and the cross-cutting initiatives that belong to no single team; ensuring leadership can speak to status, strategy, and risk at a moment's notice.

Wiz’s Global Technical Enablement (GTE) team is the end-to-end owner of technical product mastery. We build and execute role-based onboarding, interactive learning journeys, and hands-on lab environments that enable our technical field teams and customers to position, deploy, and optimize complex cloud solutions at scale. Operating across 8 time zones and 6 countries, we pride ourselves on dependability, radical collaboration, and continuous innovation.

To ensure the strategic value of this role is maintained, please note that it is explicitly:

Not a layer between the Head and the four team leaders, their direct line is unchanged.

Not the owner of team execution: Architecture, TLDD, Experiences, and TEDO run their own work.

Not an Executive Assistant: no calendar, travel, or expense ownership.

Drive the OKR Lifecycle: Partner with leadership to draft, cascade, and track OKRs, proactively mitigating schedule risks before they impact the business.

Govern the Decision Log: Ensure that nothing agreed upon leaves the room without an owner and a date, and follow through so that initiatives don't stall or quietly die after kickoff.

Build the Case (Tech Spend & Forecasting): Lead financial forecasting, budget tracking, and business case development specifically for the organization’s enablement infrastructure (lab environments, software licensing, tool subscriptions, and vendor platforms).

Vendor & Platform Lifecycle: Oversee the end-to-end renewals of GTE platforms, manage vendor relationships, and optimize the operational tech stack.

Access & Tech Governance: Manage the integration, provisioning, and access logistics for the org's internal and external enablement platforms, ensuring seamless workflows and security compliance.

Own the "Walking Deck": Maintain a continuously current narrative of the business (org, strategy, OKR status, metrics, risks, and wins) that is ready to present with zero prep.

Turn Data into Narrative: Partner with analysts to convert central dashboards, learner throughput, and course CSAT into the actionable story leadership needs.

Anticipate the Inspection: Prepare the Head of GTE for executive reviews, QBRs, skip-levels, and ad-hoc escalations by running dry-runs, producing briefing docs, and pre-empting leadership questions before they are asked.

Represent the Head: Act as a proxy in forums the Head cannot attend, carrying context in, bringing decisions back, and holding the room at a leadership altitude.

Stakeholder Alignment: Act as the primary strategic coordination bridge between GTE pillar leads and key external partners (Product Management, Product Marketing, Solutions Engineering, Support).

We’re looking for a Staff Technical Program Manager, Emerging Products to help us take the next generation of Webflow, new AI-native products, from prototype to general availability and build the execution systems that let Webflow launch new products predictably.

Location: Remote-first (United States)
Full-time
Permanent
Exempt

Application Information:
Application deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis until position is closed and filled
This posting is for a new position
Reporting to the Senior Director, EPD Operations

As a Staff Technical Program Manager, Emerging Products, you’ll…

Own the execution portfolio for an emerging product line from discovery through GA, across multiple engineering pods and cross-functional workstreams spanning Engineering, Product, Design, and GTM.
Partner with Engineering leaders, Tech Leads, and PMs to decompose ambiguous, high-risk technical challenges into clear milestones, sequencing, and execution plans that drive toward abstract goals.
Design and run the operating model for a fast-moving, zero-to-one program: pod structure, DRI cadences, cross-functional leads syncs, readiness checklists, and leadership reviews that read from artifacts teams already produce rather than creating new reporting.
Define GA and launch readiness criteria with Product, Engineering, and GTM, and drive the trade-off decisions needed to hit them, with a named owner and decision date for each.
Anticipate risks and dependencies across pillars, establish proactive risk management, and give executives data-driven visibility into where the program actually stands.
Build repeatable systems, health metrics, and playbooks that outlive this program and become the default for how Webflow takes new products to market, embedding AI tooling and automation to scale visibility and reduce manual coordination.
Coach EMs, PMs, and peer TPMs on execution craft and ownership behaviors, raising the quality of program management around you.

Requirements

About you:

BS / BA college degree or relevant experience

Congregational Operations Project Manager (Full-Time, Exempt)

Do you have progressively responsible project-management or project-coordination experience involving multiple locations, capital projects, real estate, energy, construction, or organizational transitions? Do you bring demonstrated success coordinating cross-functional stakeholders, consultants, contractors, and vendors, as well as strong skills in budgeting, scheduling, documentation, problem-solving, and written reporting?

If so, we invite you to read on...

Under the guidance of the Chief Operating Officer, the Congregational Operations Project Manager, works with Center Administrators, Leadership Partners, Facilities Staff, and Sisters to move forward the mission of the Congregation as it relates to facilities, operations, environmental and sustainability issues and other tasks.

Essential Functions

The Project Manager supports the Congregation of St. Joseph by coordinating projects that advance responsible stewardship of the Congregation's people, properties, financial resources, and care for creation.
This role will assist and support the operations of the Congregation. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and collaborating with all constituents of the Congregation over six different locations.
The role will collaborate closely with Congregational ministry staff including CSJI, CSJM, Center Administrators, Sisters, Leadership Partners, staff, consultants, and vendors.
This position manages capital improvements for several buildings, solar and energy initiatives, Sister moves, and other assigned operational projects across Congregation locations.
The role establishes clear scopes, schedules, budgets, responsibilities, risks, and measurable outcomes; provides timely progress reports and recommendations; and promotes safe, cost-effective, sustainable, and mission-aligned results.
In every assignment, the Project Manager is expected to foster respectful relationships, inclusive collaboration, discernment, accountability, and compassionate attention to the needs and dignity of the Sisters and the wider community.

Key Responsibilities

Collaborate with the Chief Operating Officer, CSJI representatives, Center Administrators, facilities staff, and other stakeholders to define project scopes, budgets, schedules, responsibilities, risks, and deliverables for approved projects.
Plan and coordinate Sisters' residential transitions, including moves from homes or apartments to Congregation-sponsored Centers; work sensitively with Sisters, families, landlords, movers, Center staff, and other service providers.
Manage a portfolio of assigned capital, facility, energy, environmental, real estate, and operational projects from planning through completion, maintaining project plans, schedules, budgets, decision logs, status reports, and closeout documentation.
Coordinate maintenance and capital-improvement projects for Congregation-owned retreat house, and several buildings and residences, while relying on qualified staff, consultants, and contractors for technical execution.
Coordinate requests for proposals, vendor evaluation, contracting, purchase approvals, and vendor performance in collaboration with the COO, CSJI, facilities personnel, finance, legal counsel, and other designated stakeholders.
Coordinate the Congregation's solar initiative and related sustainability projects, including feasibility work, site coordination, utility and incentive processes, contracts, implementation schedules, vendors, and progress reporting.
Lead the support existing energy procurement and energy efficiency projects; including utility and energy contracts, building system improvements, conservation initiatives and coordination with technical advisors and vendors.
Working closely with the COO to support the sale or other disposition of Congregation-owned properties by coordinating inspections, repairs, cleanouts, appraisals, brokers, legal and financial documentation, and closing-related activities.
Prepare concise project updates and recommendations for the COO and other decision-makers, promptly escalating risks, decisions, budget variances, and schedule concerns; perform other projects and operational assignments as directed.
The role may evolve over time to include coordinating building deconstruction or site restoration projects, including due diligence, regulatory requirements, and stakeholder communication while relying on professionals in the industry.
This role will be a member of multiple committees as assigned, including Leadership Partners, Forced Pooling and COSJ Capital Budgets.
Other duties as assigned.

Desired Skills

Project leadership: ability to organize scope, schedules, budgets, dependencies, risks, decisions, communications, and closeout across multiple concurrent assignments.
Technical and business literacy: ability to review proposals, contracts, plans, budgets, reports, and technical recommendations and translate them into clear choices for decision-makers.
Collaborative stakeholder and vendor management, including clear accountability, timely follow-up, constructive problem-solving, and concise status communication.
Empathy, discretion, and respect when coordinating projects that affect Sisters' homes, belongings, routines, and transitions.
Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence, with the ability to build effective working relationships with the COO, CSJI, Sisters, Center leadership, staff, professional advisors, and external partners.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare project plans, meeting notes, executive summaries, recommendations, and decision-ready reports.

Sensitivity to and respect for the CSJ Congregation's culture and values.
Ability to communicate effectively and clearly.
Ability to assess, define and resolve problems by identifying causes, gathering information, establishing facts, generating viable solutions, and recommending options to the parties involved or as needed.
Ability to think strategically by assessing options based on trends and conditions, as well as the Mission and values of the Congregation.

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in project management, business administration, construction management, engineering, real estate, environmental studies, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience will be considered.
Five to seven years of progressively responsible project-management or project-coordination experience, preferably involving multiple locations, capital projects, real estate, energy, construction, or organizational transitions.
Demonstrated success coordinating cross-functional stakeholders, consultants, contractors, and vendors; strong skills in budgeting, scheduling, documentation, problem-solving, and written reporting
Ability to understand and coordinate technical, contractual, regulatory, and property-related information; working knowledge of building systems, permits, codes, construction, utilities, or real-estate transactions is helpful but direct maintenance expertise is not required.
Valid driver's license and ability to travel regularly to Congregation-sponsored Centers, residences, and project sites.
Documented experience managing at least three concurrent projects with defined scopes, budgets, schedules, milestones, and stakeholder reporting.
Demonstrated experience managing individual project budgets of at least $250,000 or a comparable portfolio of capital and operational projects; experience with larger, multi-site initiatives is preferred.
Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, including Excel, Word, Outlook, Teams, and PowerPoint, and with a project-management or work-tracking platform used to maintain schedules, task ownership, risks, and status reports.
Ability to analyze bids, contracts, invoices, budgets, schedules, and change requests; identify material differences and risks; and present a clear written recommendation to the COO and other decision-makers.
Demonstrated ability to produce accurate project documentation and executive-level written reports, facilitate meetings, track decisions and action items, and communicate effectively with varied stakeholders.
Ability to handle confidential information with discretion and to coordinate projects affecting Sisters, their homes, and their belongings with sensitivity, respect, and alignment with the Congregation's Mission, Charism, Generous Promises, and Sacred Work.

Working Conditions

Standard office setting; hybrid, remote.
Engage in normal office activity, including lifting up to 25 lbs.
Preferred location near our Cleveland, OH; Wichita, KS; Wheeling, WV; Kalamazoo, MI; La Grange Park, IL locations.
Travel: travel to centers, Sister residences and other project sites as needed.

Ability to conduct site walks, attend inspections, and support move days that may involve lifting light items and extended standing.
Able to stand for long periods of time, lift up to 25 lbs., and ability to travel.
Periodic evening or weekend work.

Excellent organisational skills and a structured, dependable approach to delivery.

This position is based at our headquarters in Mooresville, North Carolina. Our corporate office is a space where you can collaborate and do your best work. Take a walk, grab a bite (or a cup of coffee), work out or get a check-up – we invest in you so you can find your inspiration.

Your Impact

The primary purpose of this role is to have single-threaded ownership of delivering Business projects that are medium to large in size, highly complex, and that typically involve multiple work streams/functional groups. This includes responsibility for managing projects end-to-end through the planning, development, execution, and implementation stages, while adhering to the PMO framework. This role may also have people leadership responsibility for more junior project management staff and contractors. Overall, this role contributes to an organizational function that plays an important role in moving the organization forward by providing large-scale improvements across the business.

What You Will Do

Deliver multiple Business projects/programs medium to large size that are highly complex from planning to minimum realization with full responsibility and accountability for the outcomes; includes organizing and tracking project details and communicating consistently with project stakeholders and personnel.
Develop, analyze, and manage all touch points of the project plan including responsibility for scheduling, global resource forecasting, managing project financials, and providing input and justification for costs and budget impact.
Own the overall performance (timeline, budget, and resource utilization) of large projects against plan and works through the project team to implement adjustments when issues/risks are identified and require resolution.
Partner with IT/Business for requests for information (RFI) and requests for proposal (RFP) processes from 3rd parties.

Control and mitigate project risks/issues by performing the qualitative and quantitative analysis of scenarios and trigger events, planning response, establishing contingency plans, anticipating dependencies affected by ongoing project changes, and recommending ways to mitigate future risks

Responsible for tracking and reporting on key metrics (i.e., deliverables, measures of success, financials, duration, benefits) and communicating findings to program managers and senior/executive management. Facilitates necessary executive governance processes (i.e. SteerCos)

Participate in formal and informal training to continuously develop technical capabilities and project management skillset
Ensure approved business cases exist for executive sponsored programs. Manage risks, issues, decisions and scope changes.
Apply deep functional knowledge (e.g. business objectives, operating model, cross-functional macro processes, etc.) in HR, IT, Finance, Stores, Pro, Supply Chain, Merchandising, and Digital to ensure the alignment, buy-in, and support of diverse project stakeholders such as internal customers, third party vendors, and senior/executive management
Partner with cross-functional Business leaders to identify and manage program inter dependencies.
Provide leadership to the team by attracting and hiring talented individuals, setting goals and communicating clear expectations, providing timely and constructive feedback as well as meaningful developmental opportunities, managing performance, providing resources and support as needed, and sponsoring and leading team members through change
Manage expenses for initiatives within scope of responsibility

Experience managing operational, program, and/or project financial budgets
6 Years experience developing project Work Breakdown Structures (WBS) / User Stories used to create project schedules and estimate
4 Years leadership experience with direct report responsibility, comfortable managing teams with 5+ people. Expert in project life cycle methodologies (Waterfall, Agile, etc.), stakeholder. management, conflict resolution, executive communication (written, verbal, etc.)
6 Years experience in program and project management

4 Years experience using formal business process improvement methodologies

or other project/program management certification

Development of custom optical systems for aerospace applications is a core business area for Quartus. Our work includes spaceborne, airborne, and ground-based systems for imaging, spectrography, lasercom, LiDAR, energy transfer, and other applications. Typical development processes start with mission objectives definition, progresses through all stages of design and analysis, and concludes with hardware build and test. Our clients are very diverse - from well-established large government organizations such as NASA to agile "new space" start-ups. We pride ourselves on our ability to find common language with diverse groups of people and to develop new advanced technical systems while meeting the budget and schedule that each particular program can sustain. Our team includes optical, opto-mechanical, mechanical, electrical, and software engineers working in a highly collaborative environment where communication and team ethics are key.

As a Program Manager in our San Diego office, you will lead project teams and ensure successful execution of your programs. As business needs dictate, you will supervise and drive the successful execution of complex engineering programs from conception to completion as an individual contributor.

Manage programs from concept to completion, ensuring that engineering technical approach, quality/customer expectations, budgetary, and timeline objectives are met

Collaborate with the sales team to identify opportunities for business expansion for existing and new customers, and ensure high levels of customer satisfaction

Champion a culture of continuous improvement by evaluating and enhancing program management methodologies, tools, and processes

Foster a collaborative and transparent work environment, encouraging effective communication and knowledge sharing across project teams and departments

BS in engineering or other STEM related field

Experience with sensor payload system development
Must be a US Person (US Citizen or US Permanent Resident)

Active DoD Secret or Top Secret Clearance
DoD related component systems development through low rate initial production
