new_jobs.title: Tech Infra Program Manager, Non-Standard Infrastructure Delivery (NSID)
new_jobs.description:
Description

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.

You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

About The Role

The AWS Non-Standard Infrastructure Global Delivery Team builds and scales infrastructure for AWS programs that don't fit neatly into traditional data center models. Our projects are tailored to the specific needs of internal and external customers — from satellite ground stations that downlink data from orbit, to specialized labs where engineers develop custom silicon and push the boundaries of quantum computing, to purpose-built environments with precision environmental controls for archival storage systems, to infrastructure that extends the AWS network to the furthest edge of its global footprint. Each program brings its own constraints, its own technical requirements, and often its own first-of-kind design challenges.

What makes this team unique is the degree of ambiguity we operate in. Many of our projects begin as loosely defined requests from internal customer teams who know what they need to accomplish but not necessarily what infrastructure it takes to get there. A significant part of this role is working upstream with those customers to develop initial requirements, define technical scope, build demand forecasts, and refine scaling models — often for infrastructure types where no established playbook exists. The solutions we deliver are boutique by nature: custom-designed to meet specific programmatic needs, site constraints, and operational models that vary from project to project.

The scope is broad, the problems are novel, and the pace of growth means we are constantly onboarding new infrastructure types and scaling models.

If you thrive in ambiguity, enjoy the challenge of translating vague asks into engineered solutions, and want to shape how AWS builds and scales its infrastructure globally — this role is for you.

We have an immediate opening for a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager III to drive capacity delivery across multiple non-standard infrastructure programs worldwide. You will lead cross-functional teams through the full lifecycle of infrastructure delivery — from upstream requirements definition and demand forecasting through design development, procurement, construction, commissioning, and deployment. You will develop and implement scalable mechanisms for tracking program health, drive data-driven decisions influencing significant capital investments, and work with stakeholders across AWS to solve constraints, remove blockers, and accelerate delivery.

Your Work Will Span

Requirements development — Working with internal customer teams to translate ambiguous needs into defined technical requirements, scope documents, and infrastructure specifications for novel deployment types
Stakeholder management and influence — Navigating complex, matrixed organizational structures and influencing without authority to align diverse teams, secure resources, drive decisions, and maintain momentum across programs where no single team owns the end-to-end outcome
Demand forecasting and capacity planning — Building initial demand models and scaling forecasts for programs where historical baselines don't exist, and refining them as programs mature
Boutique design coordination — Partnering with engineering teams to develop tailored infrastructure solutions that meet unique programmatic constraints (environmental, regulatory, physical, operational)
Multi-year delivery execution — Driving complex, globally distributed projects from conceptual feasibility through budget approval, design, procurement, construction, and commissioning
Cross-program coordination — Identifying synergies, shared solutions, and lessons learned across a diverse portfolio of infrastructure types
Mechanism development — Building scalable processes and reporting to monitor delivery health, drive accountability, and escalate to leadership as the portfolio grows

This role offers an opportunity to drive and influence business-critical decisions impacting the long-term future of AWS, working at the leading edge of emerging capability and service offerings. You must be comfortable managing remote project teams delivering novel — and sometimes pioneering — solutions across multiple countries and time zones; operating as the connective tissue between customer teams with undefined needs and engineering teams who build solutions; assessing and mitigating downstream risk; troubleshooting unforeseen implementation issues; removing barriers to project success; and operating effectively amid persistent uncertainty and change.

Up to 15% domestic and international travel may be necessary to support AWS non-standard infrastructure planning and scaling efforts.

Key job responsibilities

Work upstream with internal customer teams to elicit, define, and document technical requirements for infrastructure programs that are often undefined or loosely scoped at inception
Develop initial demand forecasts and capacity scaling models for emerging programs; refine forecasts as programs mature and data becomes available
Lead end-to-end delivery of boutique infrastructure projects from requirements definition through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and deployment
Manage project budgets, schedules, and resource plans for programs with diverse and evolving technical requirements and site conditions
Partner with engineering teams to develop tailored infrastructure solutions — working within unique constraints that vary by program, site, and customer need
Coordinate cross-program activities to gain cost and execution efficiencies; identify and drive shared solutions and reusable design patterns
Build and maintain relationships with internal customers (service teams, lab teams, engineering organizations) to align infrastructure delivery with evolving demand
Convene partners and stakeholders to architect end-to-end process flows, delineate roles and responsibilities, and establish governance frameworks — transforming ambiguity into operational clarity, eliminating friction, and driving repeatable efficiencies across maturing programs
Identify and mitigate risks in environments with limited precedent; develop contingency plans for first-of-kind deployment scenarios
Develop scalable mechanisms, standard operating procedures, and process improvements to support rapid portfolio growth and new program onboarding
Create data visualization reports and KPIs illustrating program health; escalate issues with clear recommendations to executive leadership

A day in the life

No two days are the same. You might start the morning in a requirements-definition session with a lab team that has a new hardware validation need but no infrastructure spec — helping them articulate what they actually need built. Then you shift to reviewing a demand forecast for a program expanding into new geographies, working with limited data and a lot of assumptions to refine. After lunch you're troubleshooting a procurement constraint on a boutique design that doesn't fit standard ordering mechanisms, followed by a cross-functional review of site conditions for a deployment in a venue that's never hosted this type of infrastructure before. You'll also spend time convening partners and stakeholders to architect process flows, delineate roles and responsibilities, and establish governance frameworks — transforming ambiguity into operational clarity, eliminating friction, and driving repeatable efficiencies across maturing programs. You'll regularly work with finance to secure capital, partner with engineering to translate customer intent into buildable designs, and look downstream to identify risks before they become blockers. The variety is the appeal — and the ability to navigate ambiguity, define scope where none existed, and drive delivery across technically diverse programs is what makes this role unique.

About The Team

The Non-Standard Infrastructure team exists because AWS's growth doesn't stop at the walls of traditional data centers. We deliver capacity for programs whose infrastructure needs are unique, evolving, and often undefined at the outset. Our work starts upstream — helping customer teams figure out what they need — and carries through to handing over operational infrastructure that meets exacting requirements we helped define. Our team members are builders and translators: people who can sit with a scientist, engineer, or service owner, understand what they're trying to achieve, and turn that into a deliverable infrastructure program. If you're energized by variety, comfortable building the plane while flying it, and motivated by the impact of enabling AWS's most innovative services — you'll fit right in.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering, project management, construction management or similar technical focus
Experience identifying, mitigating, and managing business risks and tradeoffs
Experience identifying and mitigating project risks in ambiguous or unprecedented deployment environments
3+ years of program management or technical project management experience
3+ years of directly managing and being responsible for multiple large projects experience

Preferred Qualifications

5+ years of experience in technical infrastructure delivery, data center construction, telecommunications, or mission-critical facilities
Track record of building program management mechanisms from scratch to support a growing and diversifying portfolio of project types
Strong data analysis skills; experience building dashboards and metrics to drive program health visibility
Familiarity with AWS infrastructure concepts, data center design principles, or cloud computing architecture

The ideal candidate is a seasoned technical program leader who thrives in customer-facing environments, can translate complex technical initiatives into structured delivery plans, and has a proven track record of successfully leading enterprise AI, infrastructure, and transformation programs.

RAID & Change Management: Can proactively identify and manage risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies, and change requests while driving resolution strategies and maintaining program stability throughout the delivery lifecycle.
Customer Stakeholder Management: Can build trusted relationships with customer executives, business leaders, technical stakeholders, and delivery teams while effectively managing expectations, facilitating decision-making, and driving successful customer outcomes.

Demonstrated experience managing customer-facing SOW-driven projects from project kickoff through final delivery.

new_jobs.description:
Description

Customer experience is at the heart of all we do at Amazon, as we strive to be Earth's most customer-centric company. Amazon Customer Service (CS) is at the forefront of customer experience, working relentlessly to provide customers a convenient, high quality, and delightful experience across all of our CS channels in every interaction.

Within CS, Network Solutions is responsible for designing, planning, and operating the world's largest customer service network - building intelligent, adaptive systems that anticipate demand, match customers to optimal experiences, and continuously improve service quality. We are transforming CS from a manually operated, reactive model into an AI-native ecosystem that makes CS a growth driver and competitive advantage for Amazon.

We're looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager who can drive delivery across this system. You'll own cross-functional execution, partner closely with science, product, and operations leaders to deliver AI-powered capabilities that detect risks before customers feel them, respond in sub-60 seconds, and execute tailored recovery actions that turn service failures into loyalty-building moments. This is an exciting opportunity to build transformative technology that directly impacts the experience of millions of customers. If you thrive at the intersection of AI systems delivery and cross-org program leadership — and want to build something that directly protects customers — this is the role.

Key job responsibilities

As a Technical Program Manager in this team, you will:

Interact with Product Managers, other TPMs, and multiple development teams to define, design, and deliver complex product features.
Manage all aspects of project execution and lead efficient delivery of large programs.
Devise technical specifications and system integration plans, and demonstrate the ability to understand and discuss technical concepts, and evaluate new ideas, design, and solution choices.
Identify bottlenecks, risks, and issues at different stages of the program. Provide escalation management, trade-offs, and mitigations, balancing the business need and technical constraints.
Drive the technology strategy, collaborate with business and development teams across the company to analyze the cost/benefit of project selection.
Engage with and influence cross-functional stakeholders and senior leadership; and keep everyone informed through regular reporting, status reviews, and other mechanisms.

A day in the life

A typical day might include: unblocking an engineering team waiting on a data access approval from a partner org, running game day testing across multiple teams, reviewing a design for a new agentic investigation workflow, running a cross-org sync with resolver teams to align on launch timelines, and synthesizing progress across multiple workstreams into a leadership update with clear asks. You'll context-switch between technical depth and organizational navigation — often in the same meeting. You'll also leverage AI tools in your own workflow to move faster: using agents to pull ticket data and surface patterns, generating status reports from project trackers, and drafting technical specs that you refine with engineering. The systems you're delivering use AI to eliminate defects at scale — and you'll use AI to manage the complexity of delivering them.

About The Team

Network Solutions is on a mission to transform Amazon Customer Service from a cost center into a growth driver by building intelligent, adaptive systems that anticipate demand, match customers to optimal experiences, and continuously improve service quality. The Network Control Center is a new initiative within Network Solutions focused on ensuring network health and reliability through continuous observability, situational awareness, and proactive intervention — leveraging AI to monitor, interpret, and act on risks to customer journeys across all channels.

As a Sr. Technical Program Manager for Amazon Customer Service (CS) Social, you'll orchestrate the programs that make social customer service possible at scale across billions of customer touchpoints.

Our program ensures the COBRA KING (CK) radar and communication systems are fully mission capable, and able to support mission operations in a dynamic environment.

This position will be required to conduct both domestic and international travel. ~10-15%

Key Responsibilities

Key Team Member: Responsible for proposing and overseeing the Subcontractor efforts, which include leading stakeholders with proposals and the development of Supplier Statement of Work (SSOW) requirements.
Monitor Progress: track subcontractor deliverables, daily progress, and repair turnaround times against agreed-upon baselines to ensure compliance with contractual obligations.
Obsolescence & Maintenance: Assist project managers in coordinating post-production support, depot-level repairs, and long-term sustainment workflows
Liaison Duties: Act as the primary point of contact between radar engineering teams and third-party subcontractors, facilitating technical data exchanges and resolving daily coordination issues. Ensure coordination and cooperation with other Customer Team members is a program priority ensuring success in meeting the Customer’s strategic and tactical objectives.

The purpose of this document is to help prospective team members better understand the role and responsibilities of the position of Solutions Project Manager at OpenDoor, WPP’s bespoke global operating model for Amazon. The role may also be referred to as Technical Project Manager.

About Wpp & Opendoor

At WPP, we’re constantly reinventing the future of creativity on an ever-broader canvas, bringing together unrivalled talent, resources and skills to provide an integrated offer of communications, experience, commerce and technology.

Over the last decade, we have developed a dedicated global client practice with the mission of accelerating WPP’s impact for our largest clients by bringing them the best of WPP. for Amazon
.

OpenDoor
is a unique integration of the best of WPP and Amazon – building on their respective strengths and visions. Whether at WPP or at Amazon, every project is an OpenDoor on new possibilities. Anything and everything can be an opportunity for our people to drive impact – for them to innovate, learn, thrive, and occasionally fail too.

The unique OpenDoor partnership model is built to deliver next level productivity, fuelled by our industry-leading approach to People, Platforms, and Process. OpenDoor spans across all WPP agencies and disciplines such as media, business consultancy, communications and brand strategy, tech and commerce, public relations, and production.

OpenDoor’s values are built from Amazon’s own 16 Leadership Principles, and WPP’s core values of Open, Optimistic and Extraordinary. By joining OpenDoor, not only are you joining a cross-function team partnering with one of WPP’s top five global clients, but you are also taking a step to challenge yourself and the world around you every day, working in the most unusual way on some of Earth’s most ambitious opportunities in marketing, tech, media, business, and creativity.

We are looking for an experienced Solutions Project Manager to introduce the delivery rigour needed to turn complex Data and Technology requirements into clear, manageable and achievable plans. This role sits at the centre of OpenDoor’s advertising data and technology delivery environment, aligning dependencies, milestones, resources and decisions across Data Excellence, Data Engineering, Business Intelligence, Measurement, Product and wider technical partners.

This role is based in London and reports into the OpenDoor VP Excellence & Engineering (Solutions Architect) leadership team. It provides the structure through which OpenDoor manages client expectations and resource utilisation, maintains an integrated view of delivery, establishes clear ownership, identifies risks and constraints early, and ensures technical and non-technical stakeholders have accurate information on progress, decisions and next steps.

No two days are the same. This is a role where you will be challenged and have the platform to flex your delivery skills and make significant impact in a fast-paced, collaborative and high-impact team environment.

Establish proportionate governance, including project kick-offs, workstream plans, RAID management, decision logs, status reporting, change control, steering forums and escalation routes.
Partner with discipline leads to identify required skills, resource demand, availability and constraints, highlighting capacity conflicts early and supporting prioritisation decisions based on delivery impact.
Create clear, reliable communication structures for client and account stakeholders, including delivery milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions, changes and recovery plans.
Facilitate effective collaboration between data, engineering, BI, measurement, product, operations, market and client teams, ensuring actions have clear owners and completion dates.
Identify and assess risks and issues, drive mitigation and resolution, maintain escalation discipline, and evaluate the impact of requested changes on scope, timeline, quality and resource.

Review delivery performance and lessons learned, then improve templates, workflows and project controls to increase consistency, transparency and predictability across the Data and Technology portfolio.

A strong track record of building and managing integrated plans that span multiple technical disciplines, teams, markets or delivery partners.
Practical knowledge of Agile, Waterfall and hybrid delivery approaches, with the judgement to apply proportionate controls to different types of work.
Experience managing scope, milestones, dependencies, RAID logs, change control, governance forums, status reporting and delivery recovery plans.
Clear and confident communicator with strong stakeholder management and facilitation abilities, able to collaborate effectively with technical and non-technical colleagues across cross-functional account teams, markets and business functions.
Confidence working with technical specialists across data engineering, analytics, business intelligence, cloud platforms, software development, data governance or adjacent fields.
Experience with media campaign data, digital ad serving technologies, AdTech, MarTech, data platforms or reporting solutions is desirable.

Preferred Qualifications

PMP, PRINCE2, Scrum or equivalent project-management certification.
A structured, accountable and adaptable working style, with close attention to detail and the ability to maintain momentum in a fast-paced global environment.

Description

Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity. The Amazon Leo Security team owns the security of product and operations end-to-end. We provide the necessary infrastructure and mechanisms to ensure the security of our satellite constellation and to protect the integrity and confidentiality of our customer data. Our team drives the research & development, deployment and operation of several mission-critical security systems and mechanisms. You will work in a start-up like environment, backed by Amazon’s infrastructure to bootstrap security mechanisms, and help instill the security culture in the organization.

Export Control Requirement

Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national.

Key job responsibilities

In This Role, You Will

Be proactive in removing roadblocks, fostering innovation, and managing multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced environment, driving continuous improvement and efficiency.
Create, optimize, and support cross-functional working groups and projects, fostering collaboration and synergy across departments to enhance security capabilities.
Manage tight deadlines with precision and drive results, exhibiting exceptional attention to detail and ensuring the successful completion of projects and initiatives.
Own the program lifecycle for large, complex security initiatives spanning multiple teams and VP organizations, including mission, vision, tenets, and roadmap contributions.
Partner with security engineers and senior technical leaders to perform program-level design reviews and risk assessments and ensure architectural choices appropriately balance short-term needs with long-term security posture.
Develop and maintain program mechanisms – including risk registers, review processes, and reporting structures – to ensure security risks are tracked, escalated, and remediated in partnership with risk owners.
Simplify and streamline cross-functional processes to increase selections velocity and reduce friction for solution teams.
Collect, analyze, and synthesize data from a variety of sources to create compelling written and verbal communications for Director and VP-level audiences, including Amazon 6-pagers and Monthly Program Reviews.
Build consensus among discordant views, escalate effectively, and ensure business and technical stakeholder needs are aligned across the program.

A day in the life

In this role you'll work with a team of engineers, managers, and TPMs. You'll help identify business security priorities, mechanisms to address the security of Leo's products and services, and will work with partners and builder teams to simplify risk mitigation.

You will influence the security strategy of partner teams to optimize security outcomes for our customers. You'll participate in hiring, development, training of team members. You'll own a part of the team outcome and will be encouraged to grow your ownership and role.

About The Team

Diverse Experiences Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?

At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

What We're Looking For

You thrive in ambiguity and create clarity for others. You have experience managing programs spanning distributed systems, security infrastructure, or compliance-driven initiatives. You understand security controls, vulnerability management, SAST and DAST scanning systems well enough to have informed technical conversations and spot opportunities early. You manage through influence, not authority. You work across organizations with different priorities and build alignment. You communicate crisply to senior leadership, distinguishing signal from noise. You build mechanisms that scale: dashboards, status cadences, escalation paths, and dependency trackers that outlast any individual program review.

Inclusive Team Culture

In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

5+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams experience
5+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing and executing/delivering product and technical roadmaps
Background in satellite operations, aerospace, or highly regulated environments (ITAR/EAR)

The Transportation Services department is responsible for providing a holistic transportation hub focused on addressing the planning, implementation, operations and delivery of all modes of transportation in the City of Ottawa.

You serve as the department’s specialist for major projects and are responsible and accountable for organizing, directing, coordinating and supervising the implementation of business and technology solutions. The projects are highly complex; of multi-million dollar value; may have a high profile with the public; are a departmental/corporate priority; may involve significant risk; are often composed of several sub-projects; and may extend over multiple years. These projects include major capital asset related projects, i.e., new capital asset acquisition and lifecycle projects; and other related complex, unique projects.

You provide consulting services to the department and the branch in the areas of project management, business analysis, process review, and the implementation of redesigned processes and new technology solutions/processes/applications needed to support or expand business operations for the Transportation Services Department.

You lead project teams through contracted service providers, consultants and/or assigned teams of staff. Under delegated authority, you are responsible for all phases of project delivery from project inception through tendering/ consultant selection/award, assembling of project teams, project implementation, monitoring, tracking and reporting on project status, vetting all project expenditures, and presenting completed results. You direct the implementation of project strategies and project work, and manage the financial and human resources related/assigned to the project. You also participate in the hiring of internal and external consultants by preparing the Request for Proposal and/or Statement of Work.

You are responsible for working with the Trillium and Confederation Line Rail Systems, ZEB, Technical Support, and various TSD teams to provide technical reviews and support through a safety lens. Who We Are

For more than 130 years, The Salvation Army has served people in need in communities across Canada and Bermuda. Building on our roots as a world-wide Christian church, each year we help more than 2 million people, providing necessities such as food, clothing and shelter. In addition, we support people experiencing unemployment, addiction and family challenges. We continually adapt and innovate to meet emerging needs and live out our mission, vision and values of hope, service, dignity and stewardship. As a faith- and values-based organization, we hire and serve people of all backgrounds and walks of life - there is a place for everyone to belong here.

Mission Statement

The Salvation Army exists to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in the communities of our world.

Job Description

POSITION PURPOSE SUMMARY:

The Outreach Program Manager is responsible for leading and overseeing Outreach and Housing Programs, ensuring services are delivered effectively and in alignment with The Salvation Army's policies, standards, and mission. This front-line management role provides supervision and support to staff, oversees program operations and case management, manages or assists with client caseloads, and addresses complex client needs. The position works collaboratively with internal teams, community partners, and municipal stakeholders to ensure clients receive appropriate supports that promote stability and self-sufficiency. Additionally, the Program Manager contributes to program development, maintains service quality and documentation standards, and ensures resources are used efficiently to achieve positive client outcomes.

Accountabilities

General
Provide oversight and leadership to both the Housing First and Outreach programs, ensuring organizational and departmental objectives are consistently accomplished.
Provide guidance and support to Housing Workers and Outreach Worker regarding client needs, complex cases, service barriers, and appropriate interventions.
Assist staff in problem-solving complex or high-risk client situations and, when appropriate, meet directly with clients to address concerns, expectations, barriers, and possible solutions.
Ensure program staff are following departmental procedures, case management expectations, documentation requirements, and established service guidelines.
Meet and communicate with City representatives and other community partners regarding Housing services, client needs, programming expectations, service delivery, and emerging concerns.
Ensure confidentiality is maintained in accordance with The Salvation Army policy and applicable legislation regarding client records and statistical data.
Program
Lead and, where applicable, perform all aspects of the case management process, including intake, assessment, goal planning, referrals, transition, and follow-up.
Develop, plan, implement, and oversee relevant Housing, and Outreach programming in consultation with the Program Director.
Oversee case management services, ensuring staff complete appropriate assessments, service planning, documentation, applications, referrals, advocacy, and ongoing support based on clients’ identified needs.
Oversee housing support services, including housing searches, viewings, client preparation, housing placement, move-in, and transition for aftercare and continued support.
Oversee program and services, including Pathway of Hope, ongoing case management, community referrals, advocacy, aftercare, and supports aimed at promoting client stability and independence.
Conduct monthly case management meetings with Housing AND Outreach staff to review client progress, barriers, complex cases, service needs, and next steps.
Provide consultation and support to staff regarding complex client situations and assist with developing appropriate solutions and service plans, including direct client involvement when management support is required.
Participate in Restrictive Services meetings and forgiveness reviews to review client restrictions and determine appropriate next steps in accordance with established guidelines.
Monitor client behaviour, intervene in crisis situations, and provide emotional support and advocacy as required.
Develop and maintain working relationships with community service providers, housing providers, municipal partners, and other agencies to support effective service delivery and client access to resources.
Attend relevant Pathway of Hope, Housing, City, community partnership, program meetings, and training as required.
Administration
Ensure that all program client/case management files are properly maintained.
Effectively utilize computer management systems to record participant documentation while maintaining confidentiality and providing statistical reports.
Prepare and submit program reports, statistics and evaluations as requested in a timely, accurate and organized manner.
Record and document all major occurrences and send them to Program Director.
Represent the organization in a professional and engaging manner.
Always treat the property of The Salvation Army with due care and caution and act in the best interest of the employer.
Human Resources
Participate in hiring, orientation, training, and employee (Include internship student and volunteer) development, provide ongoing, consistent coaching, performance feedback, and manage employees’ performance evaluation.
Responsible for preparing, and maintaining departmental staff/student/volunteer schedules, approving employee time off (vacation, sick, etc. ...) time, and submitting time sheets to the Administrative Coordinator.
Ensure that all employees/student/volunteer have completed the required mandatory training and is up to date; identify staff training needs to the Program Director.
In consultation with Program Director complete and update position descriptions and job duties for those supervised.
Identify job vacancies and follow The Salvation Army Windsor Centre of Hope hiring procedures.
Understand and comply with Union Collective Agreement.
Health and Safety
Responsible for maintaining a level of competency and understand Sections 25 and 26 of the Occupational Health and Safety Act (OHSA).
Ensure that the measures and procedures prescribed (OH&SA) are carried out in the workplace and that every reasonable precaution is taken for the protection of the worker and workplace.
Provide advice, make recommendations and improvements, and assist with the development of company policies/guidelines/handbooks as it relates to health and safety.
Work in compliance with OH&S Act and Regulations and abide by The Salvation Army’s health and safety policies and procedures.
Finance
Monitoring the program expenditures. Responsible for effective and efficient management of all financial resources of the organization. Maintain a balanced budget.

Internal

CRITICAL RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT:

Program Director, management members, staff, volunteers, and residents.
Conduct regular staff meetings to review operational effectiveness, changes in policies and procedures, and to provide in-service training.
Participate in management meeting and other staff meetings when relevant.

External

Community partners and community members who receive our services.
Attend approved community meetings. {Required to use the program vehicle when available}

Managerial/Technical Responsibilities

This position reports directly to the Program Director or designate.
The incumbent is responsible for the direct supervision of non-supervisory personnel, and has input into discipline, hiring, or firing decisions within the established guidelines.

Financial And Material Management

Not applicable

Working Conditions

This is a permanent full-time position.
This position is considered a management position for the purposes of the Employment Standards Act of Ontario and as such is not covered by various ESA rules, including but not limited to those related to hours of work, daily and weekly rest periods and overtime compensation. Salary is based on average minimum weekly hours of 40 per week and hours worked are compensated through the annual salary amount.

Education And Expereince Requirements

Valid Ontario Class “G” Driver’s License, current copy of driver’s abstract that is satisfactory to The Salvation Army, in its sole discretion, is required.

Strong sense of integrity and confidentiality with professional ethics and a balanced sense of fairness and flexibility.
Committed to service excellence, inspires, and motivates teams to reach their full potential.

Strong interpersonal, motivational, leadership, and organizational skills.

Attention to detail, problem solving and analytical skills.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
The Statewide Residency Training Program is seeking a Program Manager to manage and direct the Iowa Health Professions Inventory (Iowa HPINV) and related services through planning, promotion, and implementation. The Iowa HPINV has a specific set of unique goals and objectives that complement the three core missions of the University: teaching, research, and service. The Program Manager position assumes responsibility for developing and administering all program elements of the Iowa HPINV which includes a minimum of a twice annual update of the entire active workforce for all physicians (~5800), physician assistants (~1300), advance practice nurses (~3900), pharmacists (~3000), and dentists (~1500) for a total of over 15,000 active providers in Iowa to be managed (plus maintain archived health professionals with thousands more dating back to 1977), analyzed and reported upon. The program manager will possess expertise in Iowa health care provider workforce, education, and training as well as knowledge of database management. The Program Director leads strategic planning initiatives and is responsible for all aspects of this large, complex, and valued resource for the state of Iowa. In addition to the OSCEP responsibilities, this position is required to support the Continuing Medical Education (CME) Department in a variety of administrative functions. Please note, this position does not qualify for remote work.

Percent Time: 100%

Duties To Include

Operational and Financial Management:

Responsible for the overall development and ongoing management of administrative and operational activities of the Iowa HPINV and CME in order to achieve established goals.

Ensure the completion of a templated annual report with a visual display/analysis of each workforce within the Iowa HPINV.

Evaluate program operations to ensure the achievement of established goals.

Annually present or support the presentation of the annual report for each health profession to the corresponding profession advisory board.

Collect and analyze CME annual statistical information for the Board of Regents report and the Program Based Analysis (an accreditation requirement).

Ensure effective, timely, and accurate data collection efforts necessary for developing and maintaining each workforce database, the visiting consultant clinic database, First Five, and Primary Care Office (PCO) data.

Provide leadership, technical guidance, and support for OSCEP staff and oversees the special requests of the databases maintained by OSCEP and CME.

Implement and plan Iowa HPINV and CME program goals and maintaining awareness of internal and external trends.

Review, analyze and recommend updates to existing procedures and information requirements of CME and the Iowa HPINV.

Estimate the resources required to design, develop, implement, and maintain the Iowa HPINV in terms of cost, time, and skill level.

Formulate information technology requirements and procedures for effectively processing data in the Iowa HPINV and CloudCME databases.

Coordinate the preparation, makes assignments and reviews results of all Iowa HPINV projects and the ongoing reports.

Review with the HPINV staff monthly the reports on calls made, number of professionals updated, new entries, deletions, and transfers for each profession.

Instruct staff on the procedures for newly developed use of the Iowa HPINV.

Assist OSCEP and CME staff in the definition and solution of programming needs from the IT department or from the LMS vendor.

Make necessary administrative changes to the CloudCME database.

Continually reconciles CME credit card deposits.

Develops technical manuals for users of the Iowa HPINV and CloudCME maintained by OSCEP and CME.

Responsible to organize and support the annual non-CME “Law Student Seminar”.

Lead and manage the weekly review of CME “pre-applications” meeting and process.

Direct budget development, oversee budget operations, and assure issues are resolved for the Iowa HPINV, Visiting Consultant Clinics, First Five Program, Primary Care Office (PCO) data collection and reports, visiting professor program and other related programs within the Office of Statewide Clinical Education Programs (OSCEP) and CME.

Make independent decisions using high-level independent judgment, make recommendations and resolve complex issues.

Initiate and approve routine fiscal transactions.

Responsible for supervising the administration of the Visiting Professor Program.

Manage implementation and maintenance of CME learning management system, including training new employees on use of system as needed.

Oversee the development of report formats, data products, and price schedules for report requests from the University of Iowa and non-University clients.

Supervise the monthly billing of data sales to outside entities and following through to ensure payment is made and placed in the proper account within OSCEP.

Responsible to develop the annual OSCEP and CME budget with detail for all fourteen MFKs in collaboration with the Assistant Dean and Administrative Services Specialist and ensures accurate entry into the Strata budget system.

Perform other administrative duties as assigned by the Assistant Dean/Administrative Director and/or Associate Dean of the CME Division.

Strategic Planning

Recommend or may develop strategic plans for OSCEP and CME. Will be assigned elements to implement within the strategic plans.

Develop strategies for budget priorities.

Implement the Iowa HPINV, Visiting Consultant Clinics (VCC), First Five Program, and Primary Care Office, and develops a plan to achieve the goals of this complex division within the Carver College of Medicine which is external facing and reaches out across the state as a representative of the University of Iowa.

Prepare periodic and special reports using output data from the Iowa HPINV and CloudCME learning management system. Reports are many times requested by the Iowa Board of Regents, legislators, and senior executives within the Carver College of Medicine and must be completed in a timely manner.

Work with professors to provide ideas and information to support research, articles, or grants.

Communication And Outreach

Create and update communication strategy to promote OSCEP and CME programs.

Capable and willing to present to professional groups such as the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services, each board of licensure, advisory boards, and professional associations.

Support the publication of results in professional journals or for newspapers as requested and approved by MarCom.

Compliance

Assure applicable compliance standards. Recommend changes in policies and procedures. such as HIPAA, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), and other privacy acts regarding workforce information and birth certificate information as well as financial accountability.

Manage national compliance standards and ensure all Carver College of Medicine CME programs and commercial support of CME activities are compliant with requirements for nationally accredited CME providers.

Advise faculty and staff of the College regarding the Standards for Commercial Support from the Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education (ACCME). Develop informative documentation on the grant application process and the national standards for receiving commercial support and develop methods for sharing this information with the College’s clinical departments. Ensure compliance with national standards and regulations for receiving commercial support.

Quality Improvement

Implement initiatives targeted at optimizing organizational efficiency.

Facilitate and evaluate quality improvement efforts.

Develop quality improvement tools.

Brainstorm with staff and seek strategies to improve quality of data and ways to reduce the time requirements of creating various reports.

Leadership/Supervision

Develop and implement policies and practices of a culture that supports staff engagement in the workplace.

Attend internal CCOM and other administrative meetings representing the CME Division as requested by the Administrative and/or Associate Dean. Represent the CCOM in a professional manner to outside physicians, constituents, and other health care providers.

Conduct weekly meetings with all direct reports to optimize communication, alignment with expectations, timeliness, quality, opportunities for improvement, teamwork, and accountability.

Provide annual reviews for all direct reports.

Manage the recruitment, interview, and hiring process for all new employees who report to this position.

Develop and implement new employee orientation and ongoing professional development of staff.

Education Required

A Master’s degree or an equivalent combination of education and directly related experience.

Required Qualifications

3 years of experience with data collection, relational database management, and reporting processes.

At least one year experience working with CloudCME databases.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Leadership experience including supervising employees, excellent interpersonal skills, professionalism, customer service, and strategic planning abilities.

Ability to organize and manage multiple simultaneous ongoing responsibilities.

Three years of health care and/or administration experience.

Two years of experience working with CME accreditation standards.

Desired Qualifications

At least one year experience working with HPINV databases is highly desirable.

Knowledge of Iowa healthcare systems and organizations.

Experience with survey research, data collection, analytical and problem-solving skills.

Experience with Microsoft Office Suite applications including Power BI

Knowledge of University of Iowa policies and procedures.

Benefits Highlights:
Fringe benefit package including paid vacation; sick leave; health, dental, life and disability insurance options; and generous employer contributions into retirement plans.

Position And Application Details

In order to be considered for an interview, applicants must upload the following documents and mark them as a “Relevant File” to the submission:

Resume
Cover Letter

Job openings are posted for a minimum of 7 calendar days and may be removed from posting and filled any time after the original posting period has ended.

Successful candidates will be required to self-disclose any conviction history and will be subject to a criminal background check and credential/education verification. Up to 5 professional references will be requested at a later step in the recruitment process.

For additional questions, please contact stacy-pruter@uiowa.edu

Candidates must be able to leverage data to inform decisions, synthesize and clearly communicate insights, and apply a customer-first mindset with ownership, curiosity, and a commitment to continuous learning to deliver impactful results.

Partnering with Product, User Experience, Technology, Operations, and Analytics teams to deliver digital brokerage solutions that improve customer experiences and drive business outcomes.
Translating business needs and insights into clear requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and prioritized backlogs that enable efficient delivery.
Using data, customer feedback, and business trends to identify opportunities, prioritize enhancements, and support data-driven decision-making.
Conducting testing and validation activities to ensure solutions meet requirements and deliver the intended customer and business outcomes.
Supporting product launches through readiness activities, content reviews, communications, and educational materials that promote successful adoption.
Monitoring product performance, measure outcomes, and provide ongoing production support, using insights and learnings to drive continuous improvement.
Leverage and refine AI skills and tools to streamline and perform daily tasks.

Bachelor’s degree and experience in financial services, brokerage, or investing.
Strong knowledge of brokerage products, customer needs, and digital experiences.
Series 7 required

Strong analytical skills with the ability to use data and business insights to identify opportunities, solve problems, and measure outcomes.

Self-motivated, customer-focused, and comfortable working independently and in ambiguity.
Demonstrated ability to drive continuous improvement and deliver meaningful customer and business outcomes.

The mission of the Digital Brokerage Team is to provide an outstanding digital experience, investment tools, brokerage operational support, marketing activities, and other services to our self-directed investors. You will learn about the current Fidelity experience and investor behaviors at every touch point to share ideas with contacts to improve the customer experience.

Category

Product Management

new_jobs.title: Vendor Threat Mitigation Program Analyst - TS/SCI Clearance
new_jobs.description:
Join our Deloitte AI & Engineering team to transform technology platforms, drive innovation, and help make a significant impact on our clients' success. You'll work alongside talented professionals reimagining and reengineering operations and processes that are critical to businesses. Your contributions can help clients improve financial performance, accelerate new digital ventures, and fuel growth through innovation.

Work You'll Do

As a Project Lead Integration Engineer II on the project, provide critical Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) and Vendor Threat Mitigation (VTM) planning, coordination, and intelligence-integration. The role ensures the security and resilience of the theater supply chain by identifying, assessing, and mitigating vendor-related risks-including foreign ownership, control, or influence (FOCI), cyber vulnerabilities, and adversarial exploitation-across the Area of Responsibility (AOR). The role is highly dynamic and adaptive to command priorities; requiring an experienced professional who can operate independently with minimal guidance.

The VTM Program Analyst serves as a key contractor supporting Geographic Combatant Command (GCC) secure logistics objectives. The role focuses on the strategic planning of vendor threat assessments and supply chain illumination, aligned with the Theater Campaign Plan, Posture Plan, and Department of Defense (DoD) SCRM directives. A primary requirement is the ability to conduct high-level risk framework analysis and all-source intelligence reports, integrate them for mitigation actions into major joint operations, exercise support, and coalition logistics. As required, forward adversarial findings and reports to respective procurement contracting agencies and associated authorities to take direct action against vendor threats. Exceptional written and oral communication skills, with the ability to successfully collaborate in multi-echelon Joint Logistics and Intelligence Enterprises (JLEnt/JIE), are mandatory for success in this role.

Key Responsibilities:

Threat Analysis & Illumination: Conduct rigorous supply chain illuminations and vendor threat assessments to identify FOCI, cyber vulnerabilities, and adversarial influence risks within the AOR, ensuring mission requirements are protected from compromised suppliers
Mitigation Planning: Develop and implement theater-specific VTM mitigation strategies and risk response plans, ensuring alignment with DoD security protocols and mission-critical function protection
Exercise & Operation Integration: Support VTM planning for Tier 1 and Tier 2 Exercises (e.g., Balikatan, Cobra Gold), ensuring theater supply chains are modeled, stress-tested against subversion, and assessed during major training events
Interagency & Partner Sync: Synchronize vendor threat intelligence and mitigation strategies with USFK, USFJ, SOCPAC, and regional Service Components. Coordinate with DCSA, DLA, and USTRANSCOM to ensure a unified theater defense
Governance & Reporting: Serve as a subject matter expert for VTM policy and governance. Draft formal staff products (EXSUMs, Info Papers) and deliver executive-level briefings to General/Flag Officers (GO/FO) regarding theater supply chain vulnerabilities.
Doctrine & Planning Proficiency: Deeply understand and apply the following Joint Publications (JPs), DoD Directives and Instructions (DoDD/DoDI), and associated policies that support theater distribution security and vendor threat mitigation:
DoDD 5000.01, The Defense Acquisition System: Mandates supply chain risk management, security, and resilience throughout the acquisition lifecycle and sustainment operations.
DoDD 5240.02, Counterintelligence (CI): Establishes foundational CI policy essential for identifying and mitigating foreign intelligence threats, FOCI, and espionage within the vendor base.
DoDI 5200.44: Protection of Mission Critical Functions to Achieve Trusted Systems and Networks (TSN).
DoDI 4140.01: DoD Supply Chain Materiel Management Policy (with focus on SCRM and resilience).
DoDI 5000.90: Cybersecurity for Acquisition Decision Authorities and Program Managers.
JP 4-0 / JP 4-01: Joint Logistics and the Joint Deployment and Distribution Enterprise (JDDE).
JP 4-10, Operational Contract Support (OCS): Integration of commercial support into joint operations, including the assessment of vendor-related risks to force protection and mission assurance.
JP 2-0 / JP 3-0: Joint Intelligence and Joint Operations integration for threat-informed logistics.
NDAA Compliance: Specific expertise in Sections 889 (telecommunications) and 5949 (semiconductors) prohibitions within theater of operations.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
Effective written and verbal communication skills
Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
Ability to lead projects or workstreams
Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
Ability to meet deadlines
Ability to provide clear guidance to others

The Team

Deloitte's Government & Public Services (GPS) practice - our people, ideas, technology and outcomes - is designed for impact. Serving federal, state, & local government clients as well as public higher education institutions, our team of professionals brings fresh perspective to help clients anticipate disruption, reimagine the possible, and fulfill their mission promise.

Our Industry Solutions clients seek verticalized solutions that transform how they sell products, deliver services, generate growth, and fulfill mission-critical operations. The Industry Solutions offering delivers integrated business expertise with repeatable scaled technology solutions that are specifically engineered for each sector's IndustryAdvantageTM.

The Project Delivery Talent Model is designed for professionals with specialized skills that align to a current client need. Team members focus on delivering services to clients, without additional expectations related to business development or promotion. Their employment is tied to their role on a project, and they are eligible for a benefits package that is competitive for project delivery-focused professionals.

Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor's Degree in a related field
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future
Active TS SCI security clearance required
5+ years of GCC & Component experience, operating within a GCC logistics, operations, or intelligence environment (e.g., J4, J2, or J3) or at a sub-unified/Service Component level.
5+ years of SCRM & VTM experience, including theater-level supply chain risk management, open-source intelligence (OSINT) research, and experience integrating VTM requirements into the Joint Exercise Life Cycle (JELC).
5+ years of systems experience, including supply chain platforms or similar DoD-approved tools and contracting databases (e.g. GCSS, IGC and EBS)
5+ years of experience in DoD contracting and acquisition systems (e.g., Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE), SAM.gov, CPARS, or Procurement Desktop-Defense (PD2)) to support vendor vetting.
Able to travel occasionally, no more than four times a year

new_jobs.title: Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Apprentify Group is a portfolio of six specialist companies, each with its own culture, personality and people. Together, we support more than 10,000 learners a year and work with 200+ employers across the UK across data, tech, AI, leadership, sales and digital marketing.

As an Ofsted Outstanding provider and a specialist in AI, data and tech apprenticeships, we're growing quickly and becoming increasingly data-led in how we make decisions.

We need a Data Analyst
ready to turn complex data into clear insight, building the reporting, dashboards and analysis that help our board, senior leadership and teams understand how the business is performing and make better commercial decisions.

THE QUICK FACTS

Location:
Wilmslow office initially, moving to hybrid once settled

Contract:
Full-time, permanent

Salary:
£30,000–£32,000 depending on experience

Start:
Immediate or near-term

Reports to:
Project Director

Level:
Junior to mid-level, we're hiring for potential

LIFE IN THE ROLE

The real work:
Most of your time will be spent building and maintaining dashboards and management reporting, analysing operational and commercial KPIs, bringing together data from different systems and turning numbers into insight that people across the group can actually use.

You'll work with data from areas including learner management systems, HubSpot, finance platforms such as Xero, sales and operations. You'll also write and maintain SQL queries, investigate data quality issues and help create a single, reliable view of performance across the group.

You'll also work directly with teams across sales, product, operations, marketing and finance, translating loosely defined questions into clear analysis and presenting your findings to senior, non-technical audiences.

This is a role where your work will be visible. Your reporting will support board and senior leadership discussions, major enterprise accounts and group-wide growth initiatives.

The environment:
You'll be based in our Wilmslow office initially. That's deliberate getting to know the business, our people and how our data fits together is an important part of the role. Once you're established and settled, we'll agree a hybrid working pattern together.

You won't be handed a perfect specification every time. Requests may come from several stakeholders at once, sometimes as a fairly messy brief. You'll need to ask the right questions, work out what's actually needed and take ownership of getting to a useful answer.

TEAM & CULTURE

You'll join a central, group-wide function
, working closely with sales, product, operations, marketing and finance across our different brands.

How we work:
Clear expectations, genuine ownership of how you deliver against them. You'll have the opportunity to shape how we report, measure and understand performance rather than simply maintaining existing reports.

THE HONEST HARD BIT

The data won't always be clean and the questions won't always be neatly packaged.

You may have several stakeholders asking for different things at the same time, data coming from different systems that doesn't immediately align, or a request where the answer isn't obvious from the outset.

You'll need to be comfortable investigating what's behind the numbers, challenging something when it doesn't add up and explaining what you've found clearly even when the answer isn't necessarily what someone wanted to hear.

It's a growing business, so processes and reporting structures will continue to evolve. This role suits someone who sees that as an opportunity to build, improve and learn.

IS THIS FOR YOU?

✔ You enjoy turning data into clear, practical business insight

✔ You naturally question whether the numbers are accurate before presenting them

✔ You're comfortable working with SQL, Excel and a BI/reporting tool such as Power BI

✔ You can explain analysis clearly to people who aren't data specialists

✔ You're curious enough to challenge a brief or a figure when something doesn't add up

✔ You're comfortable operating in a scale-up environment, ambiguity included

This is NOT for you if:

✘ You need every task to come with a detailed step-by-step specification

✘ You prefer working with one clean dataset rather than investigating how different data sources connect

✘ You'd rather produce reports than understand what the numbers actually mean

✘ You're uncomfortable questioning data, assumptions or requests from stakeholders

✘ You need a fully structured corporate environment to do your best work

What You Bring

Experience in a Data, MI or BI role, ideally producing reporting for managers or senior stakeholders
Practical experience using SQL and an understanding of relational data
Experience building reports or dashboards using Power BI, Excel or a similar tool
Experience bringing together data from more than one source, such as CRM, finance or operational systems
Understanding of KPIs, performance measurement and business reporting
Excellent attention to detail and a genuine focus on data quality
Strong organisation skills and the ability to manage competing requests and deadlines
Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain analysis simply to non-technical audiences
Curiosity and confidence to challenge a brief, question a figure and investigate when something doesn't look right

Nice to have:

Experience with DAX or data modelling in Power BI
Familiarity with HubSpot, Xero or apprenticeship/learner management systems
Exposure to Microsoft Azure or other cloud data platforms
Experience with Python, Power Automate or data automation
Experience in education, training or the skills sector
An interest in AI and how it's changing the way organisations work

WHAT WE OFFER

25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays), increasing with length of service
Birthday Leave + Volunteer Day
Private medical insurance
Hybrid working once established in the role, with regular collaboration at our Wilmslow HQ
Ongoing professional development and leadership support
Opportunity to join one of our own Data or AI apprenticeship programmes following successful probation
Structured CPD support
Enhanced family leave policies
Access to mental health and wellbeing support
Benefits portal with access to 700+ deals
Regular company-wide events and team socials

THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

Recruiter call:

An introductory 30-minute call with the Talent team to discuss the role, your experience, motivation, salary expectations, notice period, right to work and the initial office-based requirement.

Stage 1 interview – Data review & interview:

You'll complete a short data exercise in advance and present your findings during an 80-minute in-person interview in Wilmslow. We'll explore how you approach data, identify insights, assess data quality and turn your analysis into practical recommendations.

Final interview (45–60 minutes):

A final in-person conversation focused on commercial judgement, communication, stakeholder management, trust and your longer-term development within the role.

Please note:
The postholder will be required to undergo Safer Recruitment check prior to starting work, including an appropriate level of DBS check (dependent on role) and a reference check.

We welcome and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, particularly those who are currently underrepresented in our workforce. We value different perspectives, lived experiences and ways of thinking and we recognise the positive impact they have on our learners, our culture and our organisation.

We are dedicated to removing barriers in our recruitment process and will provide reasonable adjustments where needed to ensure all candidates have a fair opportunity to succeed.

If you have any questions about the application process or would like to discuss reasonable adjustments, please get in touch with us – we’re here to support you.

Available Shifts:

Team 1: 0500-1500 | Monday-Thursday
Team 3: 2100-0700 | Monday-Thursday

Zachary Piper Solutions
is currently seeking a SOC Operations Analyst
to support the DISA DCDC Cyber Operations Center
based in Fort Meade, MD
. This position is a full-time
role that will be fully onsite
. This position is critical in safeguarding DoD networks and assets, ensuring robust security measures and procedures are maintained. As a SOC Operations Analyst, you will play a pivotal role in incident response, threat detection, network defense, situational awareness, and cyber operations within a high-stakes environment supporting mission-critical Department of Defense cybersecurity operations.

Key Responsibilities:

Execute cyber operations in real time in accordance with mission requirements, including incident handling, event triage, network analysis, threat detection, trend analysis, metric development, vulnerability information dissemination, and adherence to DoD Computer Network Defense Service Provider (CNDSP) methodologies.
Lead and support complex security incident responses, from post-breach analysis to threat actor identification, leveraging netflow, PCAP analysis, security event logs, and network telemetry to identify and mitigate threats.
Utilize SIEM and cybersecurity platforms including ArcSight, JIMS, CSAAC, Splunk, and related technologies to monitor, investigate, and resolve security incidents.
Conduct proactive threat hunting and cyber defense operations through the analysis of network traffic, system logs, indicators of compromise, malware activity, and security alerts.
Monitor the DoDIN environment for vulnerabilities, IAVA compliance, and emerging cyber threats that may impact mission operations.
Coordinate Computer Network Defense operations with DoD Components, Services, Agencies, and Field Activities while assessing operational impacts and recommending defensive measures.
Provide defense-wide situational awareness through analysis, intelligence integration, information sharing, and coordinated reporting efforts.
Generate operational reports, situation reports (SITREPs), executive briefings, metrics, and threat assessments for senior leadership.
Collaborate with intelligence and cyber operations teams to identify indications and warnings of potential threats targeting DoD networks and information systems.
Recommend INFOCON changes and mitigation actions in response to cyber incidents, unauthorized activities, and emerging threat campaigns.
Communicate daily with internal teams and mission partners to secure both cloud and on-premises environments.
Support a mission-focused customer with high operational expectations and national security objectives.
Utilize technical expertise, analytical problem-solving skills, and operational judgment to address evolving cybersecurity challenges.

Requirements:

Active DoD TS/SCI Clearance with eligibility for a Counterintelligence Polygraph.
Security+ or equivalent DoD 8570/8140-compliant certification
4+ years of cybersecurity, network defense, SOC, or cyber operations experience.
Bachelor's Degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related technical field. Additional relevant experience may be substituted for degree requirements.
Experience working within a Computer Network Defense Service Provider (CNDSP) environment or supporting Computer Network Defense operations.
Experience with cybersecurity monitoring and analysis tools such as ArcSight, JIMS, CSAAC, Splunk, PCAP analysis tools, or equivalent platforms.
Strong understanding of TCP/IP networking, routing, DNS, network communications, intrusion detection/prevention systems, firewalls, proxies, and network traffic analysis.
Familiarity with malware analysis, cyber threat lifecycle concepts, attack vectors, and vulnerability exploitation techniques.
Experience providing operational updates, threat briefings, executive reporting, and recommendations to senior leaders.
Working knowledge of DoD cyber operations, threat and vulnerability analysis, and Joint Operational Planning Process (JOPP).

Compensation Includes:

Salary Range: $125,000 - $145,000 (depending on experience)
Full Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), PTO, and Sick Leave as required by law

This job posting opens on 9/24/2026 and will remain open for at least 30 days from the posting date

Description

Lead the fight against fraud and abuse across Amazon's Payments business in Latam. As Senior Program Manager for Payment Integrity, you'll own the strategy, roadmap, and team that protect millions of customers — and the business — from fraud, abuse, and bad debt across BR and LATAM.

You will act as the single-threaded owner for payment integrity in the region, leading a team of program and product managers and owning an ambitious Cost of Business Waste (CoBW) reduction target. You'll stay ahead of a fast-moving fraud and abuse landscape, translate it into a clear multi-year roadmap, extend proven prevention mechanisms to new financial products such as Amazon Credito, and partner deeply with engineering, risk, compliance, and finance teams. If you are energized by ambiguous, high-stakes problems where the mechanisms you build directly protect customers and the business, this role is for you.

Key job responsibilities

Lead the Integrity / F&AP team: guide, coordinate and develop a team of program and product managers, set priorities, and own the operational drumbeat, incident response, and delivery bar for the pillar.
Stay ahead of the fraud & abuse landscape — maintain deep, current knowledge of market solutions, industry mechanisms, and emerging fraud/abuse vectors (card fraud, concession/promo abuse, instrument and credential abuse), and bring that outside-in view into our roadmap.
Define the strategy and roadmap — own the multi-year vision and prioritized roadmap for payment integrity across BR and LATAM, including fraud & abuse coverage for new products (e.g., Amazon Credito) and the extension of proven mechanisms across markets.
Drive and track projects and metrics — oversee execution of in-flight initiatives (abuse-reduction programs, card-related and bad-debt initiatives), own the LATAM CoBW reduction target, and hold the team accountable to measurable input and output metrics.
Report status to leadership — provide clear, data-driven updates on roadmap progress, CoBW performance, risks, and trade-offs to senior leadership through the established review cadence (MBR/QBR/OP).
Partner cross-org — align and influence across engineering, RCS, BRP, BAP, Risk, Compliance, and Finance to unblock delivery and scale prevention mechanisms.

A day in the life

No two days look the same. You might start by reviewing the latest fraud metrics with your team, deciding where to double down and where to cut losses. Mid-morning, you pressure-test the design of a new abuse-prevention mechanism with engineering before it goes to build. In the afternoon, you align with Product and Risk on how a new product launch changes our fraud exposure and what coverage we need . You close by refining the roadmap and preparing a crisp update for leadership on progress against our CoBW target — moving fluidly between deep strategy and hands-on execution.

About The Team

Amazon LATAM Payments Trust builds the compliance, identity, and fraud & abuse prevention mechanisms that create trust in payment transactions — letting millions of customers transact safely and enabling Amazon to scale new products in a dynamic payments markets. We own this end-to-end across the region, from setting strategy to shipping the mechanisms that run in production.

We are a small, senior, high-trust team with a lot of ownership and a strong bias for action. We think in mechanisms, not one-offs; we ground decisions in data; and we care about building things that last and replicate across markets.

Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field

Description

Business Analyst in Network Strategy and Performance owns processes & analytics that directly shape how Amazon serves customers globally. They are an analytical problem solver who is comfortable in a fast-paced, multi-tasked, high-energy environment.
